players.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens are back home for a Week 9 clash against the 5-2 Jaguars. He went 1-for-2 on field goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Loop has attempted more than two FGs just once this season, and there's a good chance his limited involvement will continue with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) probably done for the year. The Ravens have scored a combined 33 points over their last three outings, and their struggles are likely to persist versus a Jacksonville defense allowing just 15.9 points per game, the second-best mark in the league.

news.text: The Ravens placed Loop (groin) on injured reserve Tuesday.. Loop emerged from Sunday's blowout loss to the Bills with a right groin injury, which will keep him out for at least the next four games. Baltimore plans to elevate or sign Jake Moody off its practice squad to take over as its kicker beginning with Thursday's game against Jacksonville. Through Baltimore's first eight contests, Loop went a perfect 18-for-18 on point-after attempts but missed four of his 17 field-goal tries.

After catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, Tyson was a non-factor in Week 11, logging one reception for six yards. He remains firmly behind Chris Olave in the team's WR corps but could still be valuable for fantasy purposes, with quarterback Tyler Shough averaging the second-most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the NFL. Watson struggled against a tough Minnesota defense in Week 10, catching three of five targets for a season-low 37 yards. The premier wideout has still impressed across the first 10 games of his fifth campaign, posting a 52-916-7 receiving line on 79 targets. His next challenge will be a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

The third-year wide receiver hadn't found the end zone since Week 1 as he endures an injury-plagued season, but when he's been in the lineup, he's been Justin Herbert's clear top option. Unfortunately, it could be Herbert's turn on the sideline, as the quarterback was diagnosed with a concussion after the loss to the Jets. Cam Little has come up big for fantasy managers recently with three consecutive 4-for-4 performances on field-goal attempts. He's in great position to keep rolling in a Week 12 home game against the Titans, who have surrendered a whopping 44.7 points per game in their last three. That woeful stretch from Tennessee's defense includes Jacksonville's 40-23 win in Week 10, during which Little converted all four of his PAT tries to go with four field goals. Little's a set-and-forget Week 12 fantasy starter.

news.text: Little went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts during Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.. Little was able to convert four field-goal tries for the third game in a row, providing most of the offense for Jacksonville in Week 11. The kicker made field-goal attempts from 42 and 35 yards in the first half before adding makes from 31 and 26 yards in the fourth quarter. Little has been exceptional in his third year with the Jaguars, going 22-for-24 on field-goal attempts over 10 contests so far.

players.outlook: Rachaad White dressed last game for the Commanders, but did not record a carry. Perhaps his heel issue was more concerning than initially thought, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries against the Bengals, while Austin Ekeler registered seven. Croskey-Merritt's return from injury likely relegates White to backup duty in Week 12 versus Arizona anyway, though the matchup is extremely favorable. The Cardinals are allowing 128.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.

Colston Loveland will seek to keep it rolling in Week 12 as the Bears play the Lions. Loveland found the end zone again in Week 11 against the Saints, pairing his touchdown with three catches for 29 yards. The second-year tight end has now put together a 27-282-3 receiving line over the last five games after a shaky start to the season. Detroit has allowed the most fantasy points per game to the TE position.

news.text: Loveland (knee) is slated to get a second opinion on his knee injury and won't be placed on injured reserve for now, though he is considered week-to-week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.. Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four weeks. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Dec. 6 against the Jaguars.

players.outlook: Courtland Sutton disappeared from the game plan in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, failing to catch either of his two targets. It's the first time since Week 7 of the 2024 season he hasn't caught a pass, but with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, there hasn't been much need for Bo Nix to air it out. Sutton is on pace to fall short of 500 receiving yards over a full season for the first time in his career, and fail to reach 50 catches for the first time since he was a rookie in 2018. Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos while dealing with quadriceps and ankle injuries. In his place, Michael Mayer caught just one of four targets, while Ian Thomas secured a one-yard touchdown from Fernando Mendoza. Bowers' absence prevented him from building more chemistry with the rookie quarterback, but the team is optimistic he'll be able to return in Week 12 and resume his spot as the clear No. 1 downfield option in the passing game. If Bowers does get cleared to return, he'll be facing a Browns defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

news.text: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) wasn't on the field for the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.. Bowers kicked off Week 12 prep with limited listings on the Raiders' first two injury reports, and while he may join his teammates on the practice field at some point Friday, there's now a chance he's a non-participant. He's fighting through ankle and quadriceps injuries that sidelined him this past Sunday at Denver, and Friday's practice report will reveal his activity level and also his odds to suit up Sunday in Cleveland.

players.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson could see heavy volume for the Patriots in Week 12 against the Chargers, with Tommy DeVito unlikely to spark the passing game. Emerging from a Week 11 bye, Stevenson can hopefully avoid an injury designation after a knee issue limited him to 36 yards on 12 carries over his last two outings. Facing a stacked front, Stevenson will rely on volume to beat a defense that's allowing 4.1 yards per carry and 10 touchdowns to backs in as many games, landing him in RB2/flex territory.

Stevenson is now off the injury report entirely to begin Week 12 prep following New England's Week 11 bye, suggesting that the knee issue is no longer a concern. Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan had a nice bounce-back performance in the Week 11 win over the Ravens, catching six of nine targets for 71 yards and a score. The second-year pro is averaging team-highs in targets (8.7), receptions (5.5) and receiving yards per game (73.1), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan is in for a tough Week 12 matchup, however, as the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 30.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide-receiver rooms this year.

news.text: McMillan (foot) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.. McMillan's return to the practice field generally is a positive sign as he works through a sore foot, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Panthers may tag him with a designation for Monday's game at Tampa Bay. No matter, head coach Dave Canales has expressed optimism this week that McMillan will be able to go in Week 12, per Kaye.

Irving was one of Tampa Bay's few bright spots during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, accounting for 100 scrimmage yards and one touchdown on 21 touches. He ranks sixth in the NFL in touches (21.0) and ninth in scrimmage yards (103.1) per game, which bodes well for his fantasy look going forward. Bo Nix didn't need to do much in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, as rookie running back Jonah Coleman carried the offense. Nix has thrown for 240-plus yards just once all season, and he's produced more than two TDs only once, as the Denver offense has mostly been stuck in neutral. Coleman's emergence could provide Nix with the security he needs to try to throw downfield more often. The third-year quarterback will take on a Steelers defense in Week 12 that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

Luther Burden will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Burden posted a season-worst performance in Week 11 against the Saints, hauling in two of three targets for just 10 yards. Either way, he's posted a career-best 51-654-4 receiving line across just 10 games this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

news.text: Burden caught three of seven targets for 44 yards in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.. The second-year wideout has taken a back seat to Rome Odunze coming out of Chicago's Week 10 bye. While Burden has managed just a 5-54-0 line on 10 targets over the last two games, Odunze topped those numbers on Thanksgiving alone with a 6-87-2 line on nine targets. Burden still has better overall numbers on the season, but the gap is closing rapidly. Colston Loveland (knee) left Thursday's game early, however, which could open up more volume for both of the Bears' top WRs. Burden will look to get rolling in Week 13 against the Jaguars.

players.outlook: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to remain sidelined for the Rams' Week 12 clash against Green Bay. That may be due in part to the game taking part on Wednesday, but even with an extended break afterward, the star wideout is currently thought to have just an "outside chance" to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City. Los Angeles will turn to a hodgepodge of wideouts, including Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith, for wideout production in the absence of Adams and Puka Nacua (knee/toe).

news.text: Adams (hamstring) has an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for the Rams' Week 13 matchup with the Chiefs but is more likely to be activated around mid-December, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.. players.outlook: Christian McCaffrey will look to extend his touchdown streak to 10 games when San Francisco faces Seattle in Week 12. Though McCaffrey finished with a modest 62 total yards in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, he got into the end zone for the ninth straight game with a six-yard touchdown run. McCaffrey is tied for second in the NFL with 11 rushing TDs this season, and he's added three scores as a receiver. He figures to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that leads the NFL with just 3.16 yards per carry allowed to wideouts on the season.

McCaffrey was relatively quiet in the lopsided win, but he extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a six-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The versatile running back was much less involved as a pass catcher Sunday night after racking up 161 yards and two touchdowns through the air against the Cowboys in Week 10, and he finished with a season-low 62 scrimmage yards against the Vikings. Burrow delivered his fourth 300-yard outing of the season while extending his streak of games without an interception to three. He'll look to get his team back in the win column versus a New Orleans defense allowing 19.8 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to QBs.

Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his tear going in Week 12 as Detroit faces Chicago on Thanksgiving. Gibbs eventually broke down an otherwise stingy Tampa Bay run defense in Week 11, rushing 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and catching four passes for 20 yards. The superstar has now surpassed 95 rushing yards in seven of 10 games this season, and he's totaled 13 scores on the ground. He'll face a Bears defense that's ranked relatively middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this season, and that Travis Etienne averaged 5.42 yards per carry against this past Sunday.

Denzel Boston and the Browns host the 4-7 Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He brought in one of two targets for 16 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Boston struggled while appearing to aggravate a toe injury in the victory, but hopefully, the rookie has had enough time to get close to 100% following the team's bye. Boston will aim to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5 against a Las Vegas defense that's given up 13 TDs to the position, tied for fourth most in the league.

news.text: Boston (quadriceps) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.. Coach Todd Monken noted Friday that the team pushed Boston (who was deemed a 'DNP' at practice over the last few days) pretty hard earlier in the week, then pulled back a little bit, while adding that the Browns should have a better idea regarding the wide receiver's Week 12 status Saturday. If Boston ends up out or limited this weekend, Malachi Corley, Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond would be in line to see added opportunities behind KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy.

players.outlook: Khalil Shakir will be challenged to match Week 11's season-best outing when the Bills face the Chiefs in Week 12. With Dalton Kincaid sidelined in Week 11, Shakir turned nine targets into 101 yards, both season highs. With a quick turnaround to Week 12's Thursday affair hurting Kincaid's availability, Shakir could again see added looks, though against a much tougher secondary that's allowing the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts.

After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

Zay Flowers and Baltimore travel to square off against the Texans in Week 12. He caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards and rushed once for minus-13 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Flowers led his team in receptions, yardage and targets, but it was Rashod Bateman who was on the receiving end of Jacoby Brissett's 52-yard TD pass. Flowers' fantasy stock is on the rise with Brissett under center, and they'll face a favorable matchup against Houston's 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.7) to WRs.

news.text: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.. Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

players.outlook: Saquon Barkley carried the offensive load for the Eagles last game, though exited the contest due to a left arm issue. Barkley rushed 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, though did not log a carry during the final eight minutes of the narrow 19-16 win over the Steelers. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. Dallas has been abysmal against the run in 2026, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, the Cowboys have given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

news.text: Barkley suffered a stinger during Thursday's game in Dallas.. This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

players.outlook: Jake Ferguson is unlikely to suit up in Week 12 for the Cowboys due to lingering knee and ankle issues. Ferguson was having a down year prior to the injury, recording just 19 catches for 136 yards and four touchdowns.  In Week 12, Brevyn Spann-Ford will operate once again as the No. 1 tight end versus a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

news.text: The Cowboys ruled Ferguson (knee/ankle) out for Thursday's game against the Eagles, Patrik Walker of the team's official site reports.. As expected, Ferguson will be sidelined for a third straight game after he failed to practice in any fashion this week while continuing to tend to a pair of lower-body injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be in line for another turn as the Cowboys' top tight end while Ferguson is sidelined. After the Thanksgiving Day contest, the Cowboys will face a longer turnaround for Week 13 with a Dec. 7 matchup against the Seahawks, and Ferguson should have decent odds of making it back for that game.

He's a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 12 with No. 1 overall QB upside against Tennessee's generous secondary. The Titans have allowed 12 touchdown passes over their last three games, three of which were thrown by Lawrence in Jacksonville's 40-23 Week 10 win at Tennessee. Mason rushed the ball 11 times for 38 yards and logged one catch for minus-1 yard in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. He's now been unable to find the end zone since returning from injury in Week 7, and his receiving work has yet to make up for otherwise subpar rushing totals. Luckily, Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

Travis Etienne is expected to remain the Saints' top rusher during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. In his two games since returning from a hamstring injury, Etienne has accumulated 90 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) and 20 receiving yards without finding the end zone. Despite his lack of production, Etienne was received 14 of the Saints' 16 running back carries during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, suggesting he's got a firm hold on the No. 1 role. In Week 12, Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to go 5-0 at home when the Raiders visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught seven of nine targets for 91 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Fannin paced his team in every receiving category, finishing as the leader in yardage for the second time in three games. Over his last four outings, he's registered a 25-378-1 line on 32 targets. Fannin will look to stay hot against a Las Vegas defense allowing 16.7 fantasy points per game (28th) to TEs.

Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Prior to Atlanta's Week 11 bye, London had one of his best performances of the 2026 season, catching six of 12 targets for 109 yards. With Michael Penix at quarterback this year, London has averaged 5.5 receptions and 90.1 receiving yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive receivers. Despite this, London could definitely struggle against the Vikings in Week 12, as they have allowed just 27.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

Kenneth Walker has missed Kansas City's last two games with a groin injury, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson has dazzled. Walker is in no danger of losing his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield given his own outstanding start to the season, but Johnson's performance could lead to more of a timeshare as Andy Reid keeps one eye on the health of his roster ahead of the playoffs. If Walker is cleared to return for Week 12's Thursday Night Football clash with the Bills, he'll take on a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

news.text: The Chiefs ruled out Walker (groin) for Thursday's game against the Bills.. Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

players.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for a Week 12 clash against Las Vegas on Sunday Night Football. He corralled three of eight targets for 21 yards and rushed once for a six-yard TD during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Concepcion finished second on the team in targets but was sixth in yardage, although he salvaged the outing with his first career rushing score. He draws a winnable matchup versus a Raiders defense allowing 33.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.

Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. He has scored three times over that span, giving Thomas an inkling of deep-league fantasy appeal in Jacksonville's Week 12 home matchup against a Titans defense that has allowed the most production in the league to wide receivers. Thomas tied his season high with three catches in the Jaguars' Week 10 win at Tennessee, though he posted just 29 receiving yards. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are far more likely to capitalize on this favorable matchup.

While the rookie running back will return to the No. 2 role once Walker is cleared to return, Johnson's performance could encourage Andy Reid to use more of a timeshare between them in order to keep both fresh ahead of the playoffs. players.outlook: DeVonta Smith returned from injury for the Eagles and immediately received a heavy workload. Smith saw a team-high 12 targets in the 19-16 win. However, he managed just five catches for 41 yards for the game. Still, he retained his spot as the top target in the offense, and could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

news.text: Smith (back) was seen limping badly in the locker room after Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys, Martin Frank of the Delaware News Journal reports.. Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

players.outlook: Rome Odunze will be a solid option in Chicago's passing offense again in Week 12 at Detroit. Odunze caught four targets for 45 yards in a Week 11 win over the Saints, increasing his four-catch streak to four games now. The third-year pass catcher has now pieced together a 36-573-1 receiving line on 55 targets this campaign. He'll now shift focus to a Lions defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.

Jakobi Meyers has drawn at least six targets in four of Jacksonville's last five games, reaching 10 targets twice over that span. His decent volume as the Jaguars' No. 2 WR makes Meyers an appealing Week 12 flex option against Tennessee's league-worst secondary, which is allowing an average of 16 catches for 210 yards per game to wide receivers. Meyers turned six targets into just three catches for 34 yards in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he's capable of producing a more impressive stat line in this home rematch as he tries to snap a TD drought that dates back to Week 3.

news.text: Meyers was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury.. Dating back to Week 8, Meyers has been listed on Jaguars injury reports with the ankle issue, but it hasn't stopped him from being available on game days. His limitations Wednesday were most likely maintenance-related after he turned in one his best performances of 2026 in this past Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants. Meyers played 83 percent of the offensive snaps in the loss, finishing with four catches for a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets.

players.outlook: In Week 12, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He had nine carries for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Warren got 11 touches compared to nine for backfield mate Rico Dowdle, but it was an overall quiet outing for both. The Steelers have shifted to more of a timeshare with Dowdle now fully healthy, leaving Warren as a TD-or-bust option versus Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

Purdy and San Francisco's offense seems to be firing on all cylinders right now, especially after the return of All-Pro wideout Mike Evans. news.text: Purdy (ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.. Purdy has kicked off Week 12 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to an ankle injury, giving him just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the 49ers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's showdown with the Seahawks. There's been no indication that Purdy is in danger of missing that contest, but if it comes to pass, Mac Jones is available to start under center.

players.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one of his 48 kicks this season, going 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PAT tries. Houston's excellent kicker should get plenty of opportunities at home in Week 12 against the Ravens, who are giving up 26.7 points per game overall and 32.4 points per game over their last five, all of which Baltimore lost. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter in this appetizing matchup.

Jalen Coker (concussion) is expected to remain one of Carolina's top weapons if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Coker entered concussion protocol following a four-catch, 47 yard performance in a win over the Ravens in Week 11, putting his availability for Monday night's contest in jeopardy. He's been relatively underwhelming over his last five games, catching 11 of 25 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown. If active, Coker will likely struggle against an impressive Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

news.text: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that he has no update on Love (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve following Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.. Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

players.outlook: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Young performed well during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, throwing for 254 yards, two touchdowns and an interception while posting his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3%). Although Carolina has relied more on Chuba Hubbard and the rushing attack over the last couple of weeks, Young remains eighth in the NFL in pass attempts per game (36.8), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook rest-of-season. Despite this, Young could struggle against a solid Buccaneers defe

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Olave bounced back from a poor Week 10 performance in last week's loss to the Bears, catching nine of 15 targets to 102 yards. He remains one of seven NFL players to average 10-or-more targets per game (10.2) while ranking seventh in the league in receiving yards per game (86.6). Despite his impressive season, Olave could struggle in Week 12 against a solid Bengals secondary that's given up just 29.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

D'Andre Swift will aim to continue to lead Chicago's running game in Week 12 at Detroit. Swift remained the top running back in a Week 11 win over the Saints even with Kyle Monangai back from a turf toe injury. Swift's 15 touches easily outweighed Monangai's eight touches, but it wouldn't be crazy if the Bears ramped up the younger running back in the upcoming away matchup. Swift will look to build on a career-high 11 touchdowns versus a Lions defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

Malik Nabers snagged a touchdown pass for the Giants last game. Nabers finished the win over the Jags with seven catches for 55 yards and his third score of the season. Nabers was targeted 12 times, the third time in 2026 he received double-digit targets. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. St. Brown punched in another score in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, which made up for his otherwise mediocre five catches for 37 yards. He's now brought in 70 of 97 targets for 792 yards and eight touchdowns this campaign. Chicago has ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, going 16-for-16 on field goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs over the last seven games. The Chargers' struggling offense hasn't provided him with consistent opportunities, but Dicker's reliability provides him with a solid floor. With Justin Herbert in the concussion protocol, DJ Uiagalelei could be in line to make his first career NFL start at quarterback, adding a lot more uncertainty to the picture. Even if Herbert plays, Dicker will be a volatile option at kicker in Week 12 against a Patriots team allowing 24.2 points per game, 19th in the

Chris Godwin is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top safety blanket during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin has underwhelmed over Tampa Bay's last three contests, catching just five of seven targets for 29 yards. Despite ranking second on the team in receptions (32) this season, Godwin likely doesn't carry much fantasy value without finding the end zone. He could have plenty of opportunities against Carolina in Week 12, however, as the Panthers' secondary has allowed 12.6 receptions per game to opposing wideouts this season.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in his return from injury for the Commanders.  Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and the score in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. He nearly doubled up backup Austin Ekeler in terms of carries. Croskey-Merritt also caught two passes for 23 yards out of the backfield. Bill looks to be the featured back heading into a juicy matchup with the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league. Likewise, Arizona has yielded 12 rushing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 22nd in the NFL.

Mike Evans will look to move further past his Achilles injury when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. Evans returned from a three-game absence this past Sunday against Minnesota and posted a 6-109-1 receiving line on seven targets. The veteran wideout did log just a 42% offensive snap share, so San Francisco may have been easing him back in workload-wise despite his big stat line. Evans could find the sledding tougher against the Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (12.8) to wideouts this season, though Evans burned Seattle for a 7-113-1 receiving line in their first

news.text: Evans (Achilles) was listed as limited on Thursday's practice report, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.. After not practicing Wednesday, Evans' upgrade in listing one day later generally is a good sign that he has a chance to suit up Sunday versus the Seahawks. In his return from a three-game absence this past Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, he logged just 43 percent of the snaps but reeled off six catches (on seven targets) for 109 yards and one touchdown.

players.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd's role is up in the air as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Lloyd hasn't done much in a crowded backfield so far this season, with it looking like receiving work may be his only path to fantasy relevance at this point in the year. The Rams have also ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to RBs, which could make it hard for Lloyd to put together anything noteworthy.

Breece Hall is slated for a heavy workload for the Jets' run-first offense entering an inviting matchup against the Dolphins in Week 12. Hall amassed 20 rushes in Week 11, adding three catches, and has now topped 100 total yards in consecutive outings. Miami is allowing a modest 4.3 yards per carry but 11 total touchdowns (six rushing, five receiving) to running backs. Braelon Allen excelled against the Dolphins in Hall's absence earlier in the season, so Hall should produce in Week 12, even if ceding some carries to Allen. Hall remains a must-start.

RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to

news.text: The Broncos placed Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.. Harvey was already ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, but now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that he is eligible to return is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. In Harvey's absence, the Broncos' backfield will be led by J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman.

players.outlook: Tyler Bass continues to thrive in the Bills' potent offense ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. He converted four of five field goal attempts and two extra points in Week 11, his fifth game in his last six with at least three field goals. While the Chiefs have allowed only 12 PATs in 10 games, they've surrendered 22 field goals, and with Buffalo likely to test that defense more than other opponents, Bass should again earn enough scoring chances to merit heavy fantasy consideration.

Jayden Daniels did not record a touchdown last game for the Commanders.  However, he threw for 289 yards and rushed for an additional 55 yards in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. It was the second-highest passing total of the season for Daniels, and his third-highest rushing total of the year. Daniels has a tasty matchup in Week 12 versus a suspect Cardinals defense allowing 355.2 scrimmage yards per game, which is 26th in the NFL. In addition, Arizona is allowing 29.4 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league.

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

Stefon Diggs finished second on the team in targets last game for Washington. Diggs saw six looks en route to four catches for 45 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over Cincy. Diggs has at least three catches in every game played this season, though has gone over 50 yards receiving on just three occasions. In Week 12, Diggs will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

Keaton Mitchell has fallen into a depth role in the Chargers' backfield. After getting double-digit touches as recently as Week 9 against the Texans, he's handled just three carries and one catch over the last two games while Omarion Hampton re-staked his claim to the No. 1 job. Mitchell also picked up a knee injury in Week 11, which could leave Kimani Vidal without any competition in the short term for the backup role. If Mitchell is able to suit up in Week 12, he'll be facing a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

news.text: Mitchell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.. The running back was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets. If Mitchell needs to miss time, it would likely turn this frustrating three-way committee backfield into a more traditional two-man affair, with Omarion Hampton handling early-down work and Kimani Vidal spelling him in passing situations.

players.outlook: No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for

In Week 12, Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back on the road to battle the Texans. He brought in two of three targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's loss in Week 11. Andrews' follow-up to his season-best performance in Week 10 was disappointing, especially when considering Jacoby Brissett attempted 37 passes and the Ravens scored 33 points. Next up for Andrews is a Houston defense allowing 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs, the second-lowest mark in the league.

Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of Atlanta's top pass catchers during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Pitts has been relatively inconsistent this year, catching 29 of 42 targets for 270 yards and four touchdowns. He's tallied fewer than 10 fantasy points in seven of 10 games this season, making him hard to trust as a weekly fantasy starter. This is especially true due to a difficult matchup in Week 12, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the best mark in the NFL.

Chig Okonkwo continues to serve as an excellent safety valve for the Commanders. Okonkwo reeled in four passes for 66 yards in the stunning 22-20 win over the Bengals. Okonkwo has at least four catches in five of his last six games played, though he is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. In Week 12, Chig will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

Caleb Williams will look to lead a more efficient Chicago offense in Week 12 at Detroit. Williams put together a passable stat line in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but the Bears offense looked sluggish in the matchup. The third-year quarterback has dished out two touchdowns in three of his last four games and thrown for 240 or more yards in all but one of his last five. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.

news.text: Williams said after Thursday's 39-35 win in Detroit that he's "fine" and likely just has "a bruise on his abdomen," Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.. Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

players.outlook: Josh Allen will look to steal the spotlight in a marquee Week 12 Thursday matchup when the Bills face the Chiefs. Allen is coming off a curious outing in Week 11 against the Dolphins, throwing a season-high 45 times while not attempting a rush and tossing a season-high two interceptions. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, with just eight touchdown passes and no rushing scores through 10 games. Allen is a touch more vulnerable than his typical elite status.

DJ Moore will try to maintain his recent scoring spree when the Bills face a strong Chiefs secondary in Week 12. Moore tied a season-high with 10 targets in Week 11, recording at least 82 yards receiving and scoring for the second time in as many games and third in four outings. Kansas City counters with only three touchdowns allowed to receivers in 10 contests, and a mere 6.6 yards per target. Moore will need steady volume to finish in the upper tier of receivers.

TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain to face the Lions in Week 10 due to an ongoing illness when the Patriots travel to Munich. Henderson has not played since Week 7, and New England has a bye week following their travels, which will allow Henderson additional time to recover. With Rhamondre Stevenson dealing with a knee injury, Corey Kiner could lead this backfield against a defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing rushers.

news.text: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.. Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

players.outlook: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Kraft entered Green Bay's bye with back-to-back one-catch games, which was even more disappointing given he looked to finally be getting on track prior. The fourth-year tight end has now sported a 37-370-3 receiving line over 10 outings this campaign. Los Angeles has also ceded the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs.

David Montgomery rushed for a season-high 107 yards in Week 11 against the Colts, successfully returning to action from a groin injury that had sidelined him since Week 5. Montgomery handled 29 touches in a workhorse role due to the absence of Woody Marks (concussion), who has a chance to return in Week 12 against the Ravens. If Marks plays, both Houston RBs would be solid flex plays, likely working in a timeshare. Should Marks sit again, Montgomery would be a high-end RB2 with another heavy workload anticipated against a Ravens run defense that allowed Omarion Hampton and Chuba Hubbard to rus

Jadarian Price's role at running back for Seattle could gain further clarity in Week 12 against San Francisco. Though he scored his first career touchdown in Week 10 against Las Vegas, Price's 10 touches lagged well behind those of Zach Charbonnet, who rushed 20 times for 94 yards. Seattle was on bye Week 11, so if Charbonnet again gets the lion's share of work this weekend, it could be an indication that Price is locked into the team's No. 2 RB role. Both he and Charbonnet could face tough sledding against a 49ers defense that has given up the fourth-fewest yards per carry (3.55) to running b

Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals look to get back in the win column when they host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He was shockingly quiet during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss, catching five of nine targets for 31 yards. Chase's streak of consecutive games with either a touchdown or 100+ receiving yards ended at five. The rainy weather didn't stop the Bengals from throwing, as Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes, but the superstar duo was unable to establish much of a connection. Chase will attempt to bounce back versus a New Orleans secondary allowing 28.6 fantasy points per game (8th) to opposing WRs.

Woody Marks missed Houston's Week 11 win over the Colts due to a concussion. If he clears protocol in time to face the Ravens in Week 12, Marks would be a decent flex option while splitting carries with David Montgomery, who returned from a groin injury in Week 11. Marks has exceeded 40 scrimmage yards only once in five games alongside Montgomery, and that was a game in which Montgomery exited early due to an injury, but Houston's entire RB room should benefit from facing a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed multiple rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. Baltimore is giving up 29.

In Week 12, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Raiders to town on Sunday Night Football. He had 10 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and caught three of five targets for 33 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 win. Judkins has struggled to find running room in 2026, rushing 126 times for 423 yards (3.4 YPC) and four scores, but there's hope that could change in Week 12. Las Vegas allows 26.9 fantasy points per game (28th) to RBs and just gave up 133 yards and three TDs on the ground in their latest outing.

Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers, Egbuka was relatively quiet during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching two of five targets for 18 yards. The second-year wideout has struggled to find his footing since returning from injury in the Week 9 loss to the Bears, catching just five of 10 targets for 56 yards in two contests. Despite this, he's expected to remain the team's top receiving option against a Carolina defense that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WR groups this season.

Keenan Allen has served as a steadying presence in the 49ers' wideout corps ahead of a key NFC West clash against Seattle in Week 12. In his two games since joining San Francisco, Allen has caught eight passes for 99 yards on 11 targets, with seven of those catches resulting in a first down. The veteran wideout is one of many pass-catching mouths for QB Brock Purdy to feed, along with fellow vets Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and George Kittle. The team's WR corps will have to battle a tested Seahawks defense that has given up the second-fewest receptions per game (9.0) to wideouts this season.

Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jefferson has benefited greatly from the reintroduction of Kirk Cousins in the last two weeks, totaling 16 catches for 142 yards in that stretch. The star pass catcher has now put together a 47-553-4 receiving line over nine games, which could be greatly improved in the coming weeks if he keeps a strong connection with Cousins. He'll shift his attention to an Atlanta defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

news.text: When addressing the press Wednesday, Pierce (heel) noted that the offseason procedure he underwent this past March was done because he was dealing with heel pain that impacted his Achilles, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.. Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3

players.outlook: Tyjae Spears turned five touches into 28 yards in the Titans' Week 10 loss to Jacksonville in his first action since Week 6. The change-of-pace RB has dealt with ankle and knee injuries this season. The surging Tony Pollard is locked in as the top option in Tennessee's backfield, but Spears may be able to do enough with his handful of touches to warrant deep-league flex consideration for Week 11 against the Cowboys, who have been the most generous defense in the league to RBs. Dallas has allowed 16 TDs to the position through 10 games, as well as 155 scrimmage yards per game.

news.text: The Titans placed Spears (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.. Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to

players.outlook: Garrett Wilson brings inconsistent volume into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson drew only five targets in Week 11, with the Jets attempting only 21 passes, and quarterback Geno Smith has not completed 20 passes for three straight outings. Wilson has four games with double-digit targets and four games with 44 receiving yards or fewer through 10 games. With the Jets likely to remain run-first, Wilson's workload could be limited facing a secondary that's allowing a whopping 9.2 yards per target but the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to receivers due to limited volume.

Kyler Murray will look to get healthy in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Murray hasn't seen the field since a Week 8 loss to Detroit, and the Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins has essentially erased his value at this point in the season. If healthy, he'll aim to take away Minnesota's current backup role from veteran Carson Wentz.

Sam LaPorta will look to build off a bounce-back showing as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. LaPorta hauled in three of six targets for 62 yards in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, with most of his output coming from a 47-yard catch early in the game. Still, this receiving line included his best yardage total since before Detroit's bye in Week 5, so he'll hopefully be able to build on it in the weeks to come. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy tight ends in the last four weeks.

Eddy Pineiro has been a PAT machine for the 49ers of late heading into a Week 12 matchup against Seattle. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, but he made all five of his extra-point tries. It was the third straight game in which the veteran kicker has tried -- and converted -- five PATs, and he's gone just 2-for-2 on FG attempts in that span. San Francisco's offense has been so prolific at getting into the end zone that Pineiro's chances to kick field goals have been sparse, but the team will look to score any way it can against the Seahawks, who have

Josh Jacobs will look to make a return as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Jacobs missed Week 10 against Minnesota with a finger injury, and while he's had a week off to get back to full health, he was unable to practice fully on Monday. If the veteran ball carrier is good to go, he'll look to come out on top of a crowded backfield against a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

news.text: Jacobs (finger) is listed as inactive Wednesday at the Rams, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.. Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

players.outlook: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Ra

news.text: Dart recently underwent surgery to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.. Dart's ACL and PCL were apparently spared, but the quarterback remains done for the 2026 regular season after he was injured in the first quarter of Week 2 against the Rams. It's unclear if Dart could make a postseason return if the Giants are able to make it that far. Jameis Winston and newly acquired J.J. McCarthy will handle quarterback duties moving forward this season.

players.outlook: Jordan Addison is unlikely to play in Week 12 as the Vikings take on Atlanta. Addison is set to sit out another week after undergoing thumb surgery, so he'll aim to get back to full health for Week 13 against Carolina. He's sported a quiet 18-277-1 receiving line over seven games this campaign. Addison's absence should continue to boost Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton's playing time.

news.text: Addison (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.. Addison thus will miss a third straight contest due to a thumb injury that required surgery. In Addison's continued absence, the Vikings will lean on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver. Addison's next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, versus the Panthers.

players.outlook: Cam Skattebo fumbled yet again for the Giants last game. The turnover ultimately did not cost his team the win this time, though Skattebo managed just 34 yards on 14 carries overall versus a stout Jacksonville run defense. If Skattebo can hold onto the ball, he should have better luck against the Colts in Week 12. Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look to continue his dominant campaign in Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco. Prior to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, Smith-Njigba had one of his biggest games of the season, posting an 8-171-1 receiving line against the Raiders. The talented wideout has worked with QB Drew Lock over Seattle's past two games, but Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to be back for this Sunday's NFC West clash. Smith-Njigba recorded 102 receiving yards and a touchdown when Seattle and San Francisco battled in Week 5, and the 49ers have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this se

news.text: Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.. An ankle injury has left Smith-Njigba listed as limited on both of the Seahawks' Week 12 practice reports so far, meaning he has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Seahawks may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco. Through 10 contests this season, he's failed to reach the century mark in receiving yards just two times and also has 10 touchdown catches.

players.outlook: Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

news.text: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.. Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to

players.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has averaged just 16.3 touches over the Colts' last four games after averaging 22.4 touches in the first seven. Part of that decline has to do with the 3-8 Colts failing to remain competitive. Taylor has also started to cede a larger portion of rushing opportunities, including goal-line carries, to Seth McGowan, who won't suit up in Week 12 against the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Taylor remains too good to bench in most leagues, and perhaps Indianapolis' entire ground game will pick up the pace now that mobile, big-armed QB Anthony Richardson is running the show rather th

Kirk Cousins will look to bounce back in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Cousins struggled against the 49ers for the second time this season, throwing for 235 yards with zero touchdowns and one interception in a Week 11 loss. With that being said, the veteran has played just two games with Minnesota this season, so he's still getting situated in his reunion. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.

In Week 12, Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Houston for an AFC showdown between playoff hopefuls. He rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a TD and caught four of five targets for 17 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Henry also lost a fumble, his second of the season, and was evaluated and cleared for a concussion in the fourth quarter. All signs point to him being good to go for the road tilt versus the Texans, who rank 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to RBs.

news.text: Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.. After logging a limited listing Wednesday, Henry's upgrade to 'full' Thursday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Texans approaches. Either way, Friday's final injury report will dictate whether or not the Ravens' lead back carries an injury designation heading into the weekend.

players.outlook: This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

Dallas Goedert had a rather quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Goedert had just one look for the entire game. However, said target did gain 38 yards through the air.  Brighter days could be ahead for Goedert, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

news.text: Goedert (shoulder) had his right arm in a sling following Thursday's 39-38 victory over the Cowboys, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.. Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

players.outlook: Tyler Warren has been held to just three catches in two games since the Colts traded starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Rather than collecting even more targets as the team's top remaining pass catcher, Warren has struggled to create separation as defenses have focused on stopping him. Warren can't sink much lower following the Colts' QB change from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson, even though Richardson's 15-game sample as an NFL starter suggests he's more likely to air it out deep to wide receivers or take off running than find his TE on a short or intermediate route. Week 12 again

Travis Kelce is coming off one of his best games of the season, catching six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer snapped a six-game TD drought with the performance, and with 586 receiving yards through 10 contests, he's still got a real shot at his first 1,000-yard campaign since 2022. Kelce is Patrick Mahomes' most reliable option, but he has plenty of competition for targets in a passing game that features plenty of depth but no clear No. 1 threat. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against a Bills
De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

news.text: The Dolphins placed Achane (knee) on injured reserve Monday.. Achane's move to injured reserve was merely a formality after head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed earlier Monday that the running back would be lost for the season after sustaining an ACL tear in his left knee during Sunday's 24-10 loss to Kansas City. With Achane out of the mix for the rest of 2026, the Dolphins are left with Jaylen Wright (foot) and Ollie Gordon as the lone running backs on the 53-man roster.

players.outlook: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 12 clash against Seattle fresh off a two-touchdown performance in Mexico City. While Kittle caught just three passes (on three targets) this past Sunday versus the Vikings, two of those receptions resulted in touchdowns. Kittle is up to seven scores on the season, tied for the most among NFL tight ends. With that said, Seattle has allowed just two TDs to tight ends this season and is giving up the third-fewest fantasy points per game (5.5) to the position, so Kittle faces a stiff task in replicating his Week 11 performance.

CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Lamb has scored in three-straight contests, and has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two of those outings. He is second in the NFL in receiving yardage overall, and first in receptions. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth i

Javonte Williams scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also catching three passes for 24 yards and a second score during the 51-30 blowout of the Titans. Williams has 12 combined touchdowns through 11 contests for Dallas. In Week 12, he will face an Eagles defense allowing 120.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.  Likewise, Philadelphia has surrendered 10 rushing scores this season, which is tied for 18th in the league.

Matthew Golden will look to shine against a tough Rams defense in Green Bay's Week 12 matchup out of the bye. Golden was the Packers' leading pass catcher in a Week 10 loss to Minnesota, hauling in five of nine targets for 70 yards. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded a 58-853-5 receiving line across 10 games, impressing after a subpar rookie season. He'll face a Los Angeles squad that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

Rashee Rice continues to handle a steady role in the Kansas City passing attack. Over four games since returning from a hamstring injury, the fourth-year wide receiver has caught at least five passes each time out, producing a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets. Patrick Mahomes appears to be back in peak form, but that hasn't yet translated into a ceiling game for Rice, who has yet to haul in more than 88 yards in any game this year and has only two touchdowns in eight appearances. Rice will look to break out in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed

George Pickens crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Pickens caught seven passes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Pickens has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two-straight contests, having scored a gaudy four touchdowns during that span. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

Patrick Mahomes continues to roll, tossing multiple touchdowns for a fourth straight game and topping 300 passing yards for the third time during that stretch in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The two-time MVP finally seems to be back in top form after last season's knee injury, and the trade deadline addition of Josh Downs has given him another downfield option. Mahomes will need to stay hot in Week 12 in a marquee AFC clash against the Bills, who rank 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

Jason Myers is in the midst of a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's matchup versus the 49ers in Week 12. After making a career-high 41 field goals over 17 regular-season games last year, the veteran kicker is well off the pace for reaching that mark in 2026, as he's made a modest 16 FGs (on 19 attempts) through 10 contests. Myers has at least continued to be accurate, and he's converted all three of his attempts from 50-plus yards. San Francisco has allowed 24 field-goal attempts this season, tied for eighth-most in the league, so Myers could be a bit busier Sunday.

Bhayshul Tuten aggravated an ankle injury in Jacksonville's previous game. However, he reportedly avoided a serious injury and could still suit up in Week 12 against the Titans. The 2025 fourth-round pick hasn't missed a game during his second NFL year, though Tuten had a season-low 29 yards in Week 9 while playing through this ankle injury and just posted his second-lowest total of the season with 53 scrimmage yards in Week 11. If Tuten gets the green light, he can be plugged in as a fantasy RB2 against a Titans defense that's allowing 133 scrimmage yards per game to RBs, despite his injury c

news.text: Tuten (ankle) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.. If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday would factor into Tuten's potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so Tuten appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

players.outlook: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per ga

news.text: Brooks (groin) was estimated as a full practice participant on Thursday's report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.. The Panthers didn't practice Thursday for Thanksgiving, so the report provided by the team was an estimation. Given that, Brooks' practice participation over the next two days will provide a better indication of his status heading into Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers. However, Brooks would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Week 12. The third-year running back landed on IR in late September after undergoing surgery to repair a core-muscle injury that he sustained against the Falcons in Week 2.

players.outlook: Xavier Worthy was finally able to make a splash in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals, scoring his first touchdown since Week 2 on an 18-yard connection with Patrick Mahomes. Worthy caught just two of four targets for 38 total yards, and he's gone five straight games without reaching 50 receiving yards. The third-year speedster still has big-play upside, but he appears to be lost in the shuffle while Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson, and newcomer Josh Downs all get prioritized ahead of him. Worthy will try to build on last week's effort in We

Tyler Allgeier may be losing his grasp on the Cardinals' starting RB role ahead of a Week 12 matchup versus the Commanders. Allgeier couldn't get much going this past Sunday in a loss to Kansas City, managing just 23 yards on seven carries. Meanwhile, Bam Knight gained 45 yards on eight touches, and it's possible that Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will return to action soon. Washington has been pretty solid against the run this season, yielding just 3.67 yards per carry to running backs, the eighth-best mark in the league.

Wan'Dale Robinson hurt his ankle in Tennessee's Week 10 loss to the Jaguars. It remains to be seen if one, both, or neither of Robinson or Carnell Tate (shoulder) will be available to face the Cowboys in Week 11. Whichever wideouts earn the majority of playing time for the Titans in Week 11 could thrive against a Dallas secondary that's giving up 158 yards and a receiving touchdown per game to WRs. Robinson leads the Titans with 38 catches and three receiving TDs, but he's third on the team with 272 receiving yards through nine games, trailing Tate (413) and Elic Ayomanor (290). If Robinson pl

news.text: Coach Robert Saleh said Wednesday that Robinson (ankle) -- who was placed on IR on Tuesady -- is out for the rest of the season, Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com reports.. Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.

players.outlook: Carnell Tate got into his first game action since Week 7 and scored a 59-yard touchdown in his return from a shoulder injury in Week 11 against the Cowboys. His other four targets went for a combined minus-1 yard, and Tate finished third on the Titans in both receiving yards and targets, trailing Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley. Tate continues to have the highest ceiling among Tennessee's pass catchers, and the team's entire offense has been trending up lately, even though that improvement hasn't translated to wins heading into a Week 12 trip to Jacksonville. This will be Tate's first encounter

Nico Collins takes a three-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 12 home game against the Ravens. He's still a weekly must-start option in most formats, but Collins has been more of a fantasy WR2 recently despite the strong play of Texans QB C.J. Stroud. Collins' usage has been inconsistent in Houston's deep WR room, as he has exceeded five targets only once in his last five appearances but was targeted 16 times in the outlier during that stretch. The reeling Ravens have lost six in a row, allowing 29.2 points per game over that span, but they have held WRs to just seven TDs all season. Ba

Marvin Harrison hasn't suited up since Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. Even if he returns in Week 12 against the Ravens, Harrison will be tough to trust considering he has just six catches for 60 yards and one touchdown in three appearances for Houston. Fellow Houston wideouts Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte (hip) are all more likely to capitalize on facing the reeling Ravens defense, which has allowed at least 33 points in four of the last five games.

Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

news.text: The Packers officially placed Reed (neck) on injured reserve Wednesday.. Coach Matt LaFleur announced earlier Wednesday that Reed required surgery on his neck injury that'll be season-ending, so this transaction was inevitable. Reed has been contained to just nine regular-season appearances the last two years due to health concerns, but LaFleur did relay to Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that he doesn't believe the current issue will threaten the wide receiver's career. With Reed sidelined for the rest of the campaign, Skyy Moore will operate as Green Bay's No. 3 WR behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

players.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the focal point of the Panthers' offense in the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers.
