Hubbard has now received 59 touches over his last two games, accounting for 292 total yards (212 rushing and 80 receiving) and four touchdowns. He ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and seventh in scrimmage yards per game (107.8), likely remaining one of fantasy's top running backs for the remainder of the season. Hubbard is in for a very difficult Week 12 matchup, however, as Tampa Bay's defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to opposing ru

James Cook brings his usual heavy workload and a nine-game scoring streak into the Bills' challenging Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Cook collected 22 carries (on only 40 snaps) in Week 11 and is averaging 20.9 carries through 10 games. Despite a short turnaround to Thursday in Week 12, Cook's bell-cow role is secure, and he'll need that volume against a Kansas City front that's allowing just 3.5 yards per carry and six touchdowns.

Antonio Williams had a breakout performance last game for the Commanders. Williams snagged nine passes for 122 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over the Bengals. This included several big catches down the stretch, including a 42-yarder from quarterback Jayden Daniels to put the Commanders in field goal range for the game-winning kick. Williams received a career-high 11 targets. In Week 12, Williams will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdown

Chad Ryland has lacked opportunities of late as the Cardinals' Week 12 matchup versus Washington approaches. Ryland hasn't had more than two field-goal tries in four straight games, and he's been limited to just one extra-point attempt in his past three contests. That's because Arizona's offense is sputtering, having scored just 16 points over its past three games. Ryland will look for more opportunities against the Commanders, who have shown some improvements on defense this year but still rank 20th in the NFL with 24.8 points allowed per contest.

Zach Charbonnet appears to have seized the lead-RB role for Seattle heading into a Week 12 matchup against the 49ers. Charbonnet didn't debut until Week 8 against Chicago and had just nine touches in that game, but in his most recent appearance -- Week 10 versus Las Vegas -- he carried 20 times for 94 yards while logging a season-high 72% offensive snap share. Jadarian Price should continue to factor into the backfield mix as well, but there's a good chance that Charbonnet will be the leader of the team's backfield moving forward. He'll face a tough test against the 49ers, who have given up th

Germie Bernard and the Steelers play host to the Broncos in a Week 12 clash on Black Friday. He caught six of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 defeat. Bernard led his team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished third in yardage after failing to record a catch in his last outing. The talented rookie will look to build upon that performance versus a stout Denver defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to opposing WRs.

Jameson Williams will seek to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Williams led Detroit in receiving yards against the Buccaneers in Week 11, bringing in all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown. The speedster has now posted a 36-611-6 receiving line across 10 games, and he's logged 50 or more yards in four of his last five outings. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

Xavier Hutchinson has topped 30 yards just once in Houston's last five games. He had a three-game touchdown streak to buoy his stat line during that stretch, but the scoring binge was likely fool's gold for a fourth-year player who had just three career TDs prior to that streak, which was snapped in the Week 11 win over Indianapolis. Starting a new scoring streak won't be easy in Week 12 against a Ravens defense that has held WRs to just seven touchdowns. While the Ravens are giving up 162 yards per game to the position, Hutchinson is competing for targets with Nico Collins and Tank Dell, as w

Isaiah Likely had an unexpectedly quiet game for the Giants last week.  Despite the win, Likely managed just one grab for 35 yards. he had a season-low three targets for the contest.  Likely is having a breakout campaign for the G-Men overall, though, so expect a return to normalcy in Week 12 versus the Colts. Indy is allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Colts have also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

news.text: Likely (groin) was listed as limited on Thursday's practice report, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.. Likely suffered a strained groin last Friday, and while it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's win against the Jaguars, he gathered in just one of three targets for 35 yards on a 76 percent snap share. He now has managed back-to-back limited listings to begin Week 12 prep, and Friday's practice report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.

players.outlook: Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

DeMario Douglas has an uncertain role ahead of the Patriots' Week 12 matchup against the Chargers. Douglas was held to a season-low three-yard catch in Week 10 with Drake Maye injured on the opening drive. The Week 11 bye is likely not sufficient for Douglas and new QB Tommy DeVito to develop a rapport. The Chargers offer an exploitable matchup, allowing 9.1 yards per target, but Douglas' volume will be in question, suggesting a wait-and-see approach is prudent.

Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Robinson has been one of fantasy's most productive running backs this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in scrimmage yards (120.7) and touches (22.0) per game. Despite the Falcons' recent offensive struggles, Robinson has continued to be impactful for fantasy purposes, averaging 17.3 points per game over the team's last three games. However, he could struggle against a strong Vikings defense that's allowed just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this sea

Tony Pollard rushed for 110 yards in the Titans' Week 11 loss to Dallas. His touchdown streak was halted at three games and six TDs, but he's up to 501 scrimmage yards over the past four games. Tennessee's entire offense has picked up the pace over that span, with QB Cam Ward stringing together his best three games of the season. Pollard faces a daunting Week 12 matchup against Jacksonville's elite run defense, but he navigated this matchup effectively in Week 10, setting season highs across the board with eight catches for 66 yards and a TD on nine targets to complement his modest 33 rushing

Trey McBride stands as perhaps the Cardinals' last healthy reliable producer ahead of a battle against the Commanders in Week 12. With WR Michael Wilson (neck) done for the season and RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) still on IR, McBride has been counted on to carry the offense. The star tight end has mostly held up, including in a loss to Kansas City this past Sunday when he posted a 9-54-0 line on a team-high 14 targets. It remains to be seen if McBride will be catching passes from rookie Carson Beck (back) or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson this weekend, but either way he'll likely be the team's o

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

Jonah Coleman cemented himself as the Broncos' No. 1 running back with a stunning performance in a Week 11 win over the Raiders. The fourth-round rookie romped for 129 scrimmage yards on 28 touches while scoring three rushing touchdowns, extending his streak of games with at least one score to three. Coleman appears capable of handling a bell-cow workload and a three-down role, but he could face competition for passing-down snaps once RJ Harvey is cleared to return from a knee injury. Coleman will face a Steelers defense in Week 12 that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs

Dak Prescott scored five touchdowns for the second-straight game for the Cowboys. Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, while rushing for another score in the 51-30 thrashing of the Titans. Prescott has thrown for over 300 yards in three-straight contests, and now has 25 passing touchdowns on the season. That places him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ni

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if

Jared Goff will look to keep Detroit rolling in Week 12 against the Bears. Goff put together another solid performance in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, slinging for 278 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran now sports a 20:4 TD:INT and has thrown for 2,716 yards across 10 games. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy quarterbacks so far this year and allowed 222 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception to Tyler Shough this past Sunday.

Blake Corum will look to build on a season-best performance when the Rams host the Packers in Week 12. Corum rumbled for a season-high 100 rushing yards and a touchdown in Week 10 against Arizona while adding three catches for 19 yards. He should be fresh with Los Angeles having been on bye in Week 12, and Corum could be even more important than usual if backfield mate Kyren Williams' sore toe inhibits him at all. Both ball carriers could be productive against a Green Bay defense that ranks 26th in the NFL with 21.1 fantasy points per game allowed to RBs this season.

Spencer Shrader's stellar start is a distant memory. The struggling kicker has gone just 6-for-10 on field-goal attempts over the past five games after making all 18 of his attempts through Week 6. Indianapolis has switched QBs from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson after dropping six of its last seven games, but moving the ball will likely remain difficult for the Colts' underwhelming offense in Week 12 against the Giants, who allow the seventh-fewest scrimmage yards (310.5) and 12th-fewest points (21.4) per game. Shrader is a risky Week 12 fantasy option.

Tre Tucker has yet to get on the same page as new starting quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Tucker recorded 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he was able to haul in just two for 50 yards. Meanwhile, Jack Bech posted an 8-88-1 line on nine targets, and he may be making a push to replace Tucker as the team's No. 1 wide receiver. Tucker will attempt to prove he deserves to continue seeing high volume from Mendoza in Week 12 against a Browns secondary that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Dominic Zvada missed yet another field goal last game for the Giants. The inconsistent rookie actually connected on three field goals from 40-plus yards out, but somehow missed a 32-yarder in the 23-18 win over the Jags. It was the seventh miss of the season for Zvada, which is tied for the league-lead. Zvada still appears to have his job heading into Week 12 versus the Colts, though. Indy is allowing 27 points per game, which is 28th in the NFL.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that

Aaron Jones will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jones rushed the ball eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown, and he caught one pass for 13 yards in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. While the committee approach of Minnesota's backfield hasn't allowed for dominance for him or Jordan Mason, Jones has been the one to find the end zone more often. Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

Parker Washington had a career-high 152 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven receptions against the Titans in Week 10, and he'll face the AFC South's cellar-dwellers again in Week 12, this time in Jacksonville. Another fantasy WR1 performance is on the table for Washington against Tennessee's reeling secondary, which has allowed the most catches and receiving yards to wideouts this season. The Titans are giving up 16 catches for 210 yards and 1.1 TDs per game to WRs, while Washington leads the Jaguars with a 44-748-6 receiving line through 10 games, with two of his three 100-yard receiving

news.text: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.. Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game i

players.outlook: Deebo Samuel continues to be a Swiss Army knife for San Francisco heading into a Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks. In this past Sunday's win over the Vikings, Samuel recorded two carries for 27 yards, caught three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards. While that might not add up to substantial fantasy production, Samuel's skill set could be invaluable for the 49ers against a tough defense like the Seahawks'. Seattle has given up the fewest yards per target (5.89) to wideouts this season, so San Francisco may look to be creative in order to push the ball downfiel

J.J. McCarthy tossed a touchdown pass for the second-straight game for the Giants.  However, it was only the third touchdown pass in five outings for McCarthy. He has rushed for at least 22 yards in four of those five contests, though has yet to find the end zone with his legs. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense that has struggled mightily in 2026. Indianapolis currently ranks in the bottom five in the NFL in terms of rushing yards allowed, passing touchdowns surrendered and overall points yielded this season.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

Ollie Gordon will look to repeat prior success when the Dolphins face the Jets for the second time this year in Week 12. He drew only 11 carries in Week 11, his lowest total since Week 4, but burst through for 6.3 yards per carry, also his best mark since Week 4. Gordon rushed for 103 yards on 25 carries against the Jets in Week 7. Their defense has allowed 4.6 yards per carry and eight rushing scores through 11 games, surrendering an additional four touchdown receptions, and Gordon is more involved in the passing game with McCord under center.

T.J. Hockenson figures to be a top option in Minnesota's passing offense against the Falcons in Week 12. Hockenson was busy again in his return to the field against the 49ers in Week 11, catching six of seven targets for 55 yards. The veteran has now brought in four of more catches in each of his last four games. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs so far this season.

Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 12. He brought in two of three targets for 43 yards, including a beautiful over-the-shoulder 31-yard touchdown, during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) were both held in check, but Higgins was able to reach the end zone for the sixth time in his last five games. He will aim to tally his first 100-yard outing since Week 8 against a New Orleans defense giving up 28.6 fantasy points per game (eighth) to WRs.

news.text: After not practicing Friday, Higgins (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.. Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.

players.outlook: Brandon Aubrey made one field goal and six extra points last game for the Cowboys. Dallas destroyed Tennessee by a score of 51-30, though all the touchdowns left Aubrey with only a modest kicking performance. In fact, it was the first time in five outings that he failed to kick multiple field goals in a single game. In Week 12, Dallas will face division rival Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 23.7 points per tilt, which is 18th in the NFL.

Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Saints to town for an interconference showdown in Week 12. He had six carries for six yards and caught five of eight targets for 30 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Brown watched as Samaje Perine erupted for 97 scrimmage yards on 10 touches, as Brown was unable to build upon his two-TD performance from the previous outing. Next up is a juicy matchup against New Orleans' 31st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.5) to opposing RBs.

Jordan Love will travel to take on the Rams in a Week 12 matchup for Green Bay out of the bye. Love and the Packers went into their off week with many questions, with the starting quarterback throwing for 220 yards and a 1:1 TD:INT versus Minnesota in Week 10. Love has still put together an impressive first half of the season, with multiple touchdowns in all but one game and 2,838 passing yards across 10 weeks. Los Angeles has ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign, so Love might have his work cut out for him to return to dominance.

Keon Coleman doesn't draw enough of Josh Allen's attention to be a reliable fantasy option when the Bills face the Chiefs in Week 12. Despite Allen throwing a season-high 45 times in Week 11, Coleman brought in only two of four targets, finishing with 17 yards, tying a four-game high. Kansas City is allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target and has given up only three touchdown catches to wideouts. This is not the week for Coleman to emerge.

C.J. Stroud has thrown 16 touchdown passes in his last five games as he tries to carry the Texans and keep their playoff hopes alive. The surging QB is a top-10 fantasy option at his position in Week 12 against a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed at least 33 points in four of the past five games. Baltimore is on a six-game losing streak, which makes this game close to a must-win for the 4-6 Texans, who trail the Browns and Steelers by two games apiece and the Patriots by one game in the battle for the last two AFC wild-card spots. Houston has gotten subpar efficiency from its RBs, who ar

Matthew Stafford emerges from the Rams' bye with the prospect of facing Green Bay in Week 12 still without either of his two top wideouts. Davante Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to come off IR this week, and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss the remainder of the campaign. Stafford was able to guide Los Angeles to a win without both stars in Week 10 against Arizona, throwing for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception, but he'll likely face a tougher challenge this week. Whereas the Cardinals rank 30th in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks, the Packe

Mason Taylor's involvement in the Jets' low-volume passing game remains limited ahead of a Week 12 clash with the Dolphins. He has been held to 25 yards or fewer in seven of nine games this season, drawing just 31 targets on the year. He provided a spike week of five catches, 62 yards, and two touchdowns against Miami in Week 7, but his usage and form don't portend a repeat against a defense that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to tight ends but only four additional touchdowns outside of Taylor's prior effort.

Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the clear No. 1 option in the Chargers' backfield. Over the last three games, the second-year running back has turned 49 carries into 254 rushing yards and a touchdown, averaging a robust 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell picked up a knee injury in a Week 11 loss to the Jets, which could leave Kimani Vidal as the primary backup. Hampton will look to keep surging in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Malik Washington brings steady but middling production for the Dolphins into a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. For the fourth time in five games since Miami's Week 6 bye, Washington caught three passes in Week 11, finishing with just 30 yards. With Caleb Douglas emerging as Miami's top option, their low-success passing game hasn't proven capable of sustaining multiple receivers. The Jets are allowing 7.6 yard per target, ranking towards the bottom portion of the middle-tier, not suggesting Washington can break out on limited opportunities.

Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are in Houston for an AFC clash in Week 12. Despite playing 49% of the offensive snaps during Baltimore's Week 11 defeat, Lane was not targeted in the passing game. One week after earning a career-high 11 targets in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, the rookie receiver was unable to establish further chemistry with his new QB. Lane could take advantage of a Texans defense allowing 35.7 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs, but he's best left on fantasy benches for now.

Tanner McKee continues to struggle under center for the Eagles, though admittedly he is working with limited help. Though running back Saquon Barkley returned from injury in the loss to Washington, staring wideouts Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks remained sidelined, and the right side of the offensive line is still a work in progress. McKee had two turnovers while failing to throw a touchdown against the Commanders. In Week 9, McKee will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. The G-Men are allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. However, New York has yielde

Rudolph is expected to return as the clipboard holder in Pittsburgh, with Aaron Rodgers back as the starter. The veteran quarterback has never appeared in more than 10 games in a single season and made just one start in 2025 (he threw for 171 yards and one TD on 31 attempts). Rudolph has thrown 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his six-year career, and isn't much of a rushing threat (career 75-209-1). The 31-year-old wouldn't even be a QB2 option in superflex if called on to start.
Malik Willis is headed for the IR after an MRI revealed a core-muscle injury. The diagnosis will sideline him through at least Week 13. Kyle McCord is poised to take over under center.

news.text: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that, at this time, surgery to address Willis' groin/core injury is not foreseen, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.. That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

players.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bucky Irving, Gainwell has emerged as one of the top playmakers on this Buccaneers offense. Over the team's last four contests, Gainwell has averaged 90.8 scrimmage yards per game but hasn't found the end zone. He could be a valuable fantasy asset in Week 12, as Tampa Bay is set to face a Carolina defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) in the NFL this year.

Baker Mayfield is expected to continue leading Tampa Bay's offense during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield battled through foot and thumb injuries during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, throwing for 187 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has struggled this season, averaging just 158.4 passing yards per game while accounting for six total touchdowns and seven turnovers in seven games. He will likely struggle against the Panthers' defense in Week 12, as Carolina has allowed just 19.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

Anthony Richardson is taking over as the Colts' starting QB, beginning with the team's Week 12 home game against the Giants, after Indianapolis released former starter Daniel Jones. Richardson is worth rostering in almost all formats given his immense rushing upside. The 2023 fourth overall pick out of Florida has 635 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns on the ground in 15 NFL starts, but he has averaged just 159 passing yards with an 11:13 TD:INT ratio in those games. Richardson has plenty of arm strength but lacks accuracy, with a career completion rate of 50.6%. Don't expect him to move the bal

Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens visit the Texans in Week 12. He threw for 276 yards with one TD and one INT and rushed twice for seven yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Brissett has plenty of talented targets available to him, and it appears the Ravens are willing to continue letting it fly on offense. He'll look to get his first win with his new club versus a Houston defense allowing 20.9 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

Alvin Kamara will likely play a minimal offensive role during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Despite finding the end zone during the Week 11 loss to the Saints, Kamara played just eight offensive snaps while Travis Etienne and CJ Donaldson each played 32. Additionally, Kamara has received just seven touches over the Saints' last two games, suggesting his role in the offense has diminished. Expect Kamara to have minimal value in Week 12 against a Bengals defense that's given up just 294 receiving yards to RBs through nine games this year.

Michael Penix is expected to continue leading the Falcons' offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Penix has really struggled over Atlanta's last three games, averaging just 191 passing yards per game while throwing just one touchdown and six interceptions during that stretch. He will likely continue to struggle against a great Vikings defense in Week 12, as Minnesota has allowed just 14.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. However, there is some hope for Penix, with Brock Purdy putting up 35 points while throwing for 255 yards and three touchdowns agai

Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Raiders in a Week 12 showdown on Sunday Night Football. During Cleveland's Week 10 victory, he threw for 312 yards (25-of-40) with zero TDs and one INT, and had eight carries for 49 yards and a TD. Watson spread the ball around to nine different receivers to help lead a comeback win, but he's now failed to record a TD pass in four straight outings. That streak could come to an end as Las Vegas allows 23.8 fantasy points per game (29th) to QBs and has given up the second-most passing TDs (23) this season.

Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to return as Seattle's starting QB for the team's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco. Darnold missed the Seahawks' past two games due to the pair of injuries, but he's line to return following the club's Week 11 bye. If that does indeed happen, Drew Lock is likely to return to the backup role despite playing well during Darnold's absence. Whoever ultimately starts will face a 49ers defense that has given up an 89.1 QB rating this season to rank 15th in the NFL in that category.

Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

news.text: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.. Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entr

players.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 12 meeting with the Texans. He had six carries for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Hill lost a fumble but was otherwise very productive with his 10 total touches, as he's now recorded two TDs in his last three games. He'll aim to keep contributing against a Houston defense allowing 21.4 fantasy points per game (14th) to RBs.

Tyler Shough is expected to continue leading the Saints' offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Shough has been held in check over the last two weeks, averaging 204.5 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception per game during that stretch. Despite this, Shough ranks second in the NFL in pass attempts per game (38.5), suggesting more fantasy value is imminent as the season progresses. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 12 matchup against a Bengals defense that's allowed 20.9 fantasy points per game through nine contests this season.

Jameis Winston was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy last game for the Giants. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt, throwing for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

Kyle Monangai will look to get more opportunities as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Monangai was quiet in his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, carrying the ball eight times for just 18 yards. The second-year ball carrier could be in line for a ramped up role in the upcoming away matchup, but D'Andre Swift currently looks to have the RB1 role in his grasp. Detroit's defense has ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

Kaelon Black will face another tough run defense when the 49ers host the Seahawks in Week 12. Black couldn't do much against the Vikings' vaunted defense this past Sunday, gaining just eight yards on six carries while adding seven yards on his lone reception. He also saw a three-game streak of double-digit touches snapped, but the rookie maintained a steady 30% offensive snap share. Black and the 49ers' running game as a whole should be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranks seventh in the NFL with 15.1 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs.

Drew Lock will likely return to being Seattle's backup quarterback in Week 12 versus San Francisco. Lock started each of the Seahawks past two games before the team's Week 11 bye and led his team to a pair of wins, compiling 415 passing yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. However, Sam Darnold (quad/ribs)  is expected to return to action in Week 12 following an injury layoff, and he'll presumably reclaim his starting role from Lock. The 49ers have been middle-of-the-pack in most categories against the pass this season, but Lock probably isn't going to get a chance to test their de

news.text: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.. Lock has been working through an elbow issue to his throwing arm since late October, which has limited his participation in the first two practices of Week 12 prep. He started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye, but is expected to revert to backup duties provided Sam Darnold (quadriceps) is cleared to start against the 49ers on Sunday. If Lock isn't available to play against San Francisco, then Jalen Milroe (illness) would be in line to operate as Seattle's QB2 behind Darnold.

players.outlook: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Sampson was out-touched 13-8 by starter Quinshon Judkins, but Sampson continues to push closer to an even timeshare. Sampson will look to contribute more versus a Las Vegas defense allowing 26.9 fantasy points per game to RBs, the fifth most in the league.

Rico Dowdle and the Steelers welcome the Broncos to town for a Week 12 meeting on Black Friday. He rushed five times for 15 yards and hauled in four of five targets for 19 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Dowdle again trailed Jaylen Warren in backfield touches, as the former earned nine to the latter's 11. Dowdle will look to make the most of his opportunities against Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

Kyle McCord hasn't shown he can move an NFL offense ahead of the Dolphins' Week 12 matchup with the Jets. In two games as Miami's starter, McCord has been forced to throw 65 times, completing just 29 for 311 yards, and remains without a touchdown. The Jets have allowed 19 touchdown passes through 11 games and have only two interceptions, so if McCord can play mistake-free in Week 12, he'll have a chance for his best outing, though still remaining near or at the bottom of quarterback rankings.

Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers look to remain undefeated at home when they host the Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12. He threw for 227 yards (30-of-44) with one TD and no INTs and rushed five times for 29 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. The production was the most for Rodgers since he put up 253 passing yards in Week 6, as the Steelers' offense continued to underwhelm in a second straight defeat. The 42-year-old signal-caller will attempt to be more effective versus a Denver defense allowing 22.0 fantasy points per game (T-24th) to opposing QBs.

Sanders enters his second NFL season set to back up Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild card and is likely to earn some

Geno Smith brings low-volume but surging efficiency into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. While he hasn't topped 176 passing yards in three straight games and has failed to complete more than 18 attempts, Smith is coming off his third three-touchdown pass outing in Week 11. With the Jets preferring a run-first approach paired with an unhealthy receiving corps, Smith is not a fantasy option against a mid-tier secondary that's allowing 7.7 yards per attempt.

Joe Milton guided the Eagles to victory last game, though his numbers were rather pedestrian. Milton threw for 141 yards and rushed for just seven more in the 19-16 win over the Steelers. He has yet to throw a touchdown through two starts. That could change in Week 12, though, as he faces the porous defense of his former squad, the Dallas Cowboys. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

Carson Beck may be able to return from a back injury to start at quarterback for Arizona in Week 12 against Washington. Beck had been in line to make his second NFL start this past Sunday against the Chiefs, but a bout of back spasms held him out of action. Should Beck be past the issue by this Sunday, he's likely to reclaim the starting QB role from veteran journeyman Josh Johnson. If Beck plays, he could find success versus a Commanders defense that ranks 27th in the NFL with 23.3 fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

Daniel Jones remains without a multi-TD performance this season, and he has minimal talent to work with after Indianapolis' trade-deadline selloff. One of his three wins in 10 tries came in Week 3 against the Texans, when Jones threw for 235 yards, one touchdown, and one interception against a Houston secondary that's allowing the sixth-most passing yards per game this season. Even repeating that stat line will be a challenge for Jones in the Week 11 rematch on the road, considering he's averaging just 183 passing yards per game and no remaining pass catcher on the Colts has more than 276 rece

Justin Herbert threw multiple touchdowns for the first time this season in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, but he was placed in the concussion protocol after getting sacked six times. Both scores went to Ladd McConkey, but it was still an overall poor performance from Herbert, who failed to reach 200 passing yards for a third straight game. His 8:11 TD:INT ratio through 10 contests is awful, and an injury-ravaged offensive line has allowed Herbert to get sacked a league-high 39 times. If Herbert is cleared through the protocol in time, he'll face a Patriots defense in Week 12 that rank

news.text: Herbert (concussion) was officially deemed a non-participant in Thursday's practice.. Herbert, who landed in the NFL's concussion protocol in the wake of this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, didn't practice Wednesday, either. He thus is looking iffy, at best, for this weekend's game against the Patriots, especially given the Chargers' 1-9 record. If Herbert is inactive versus New England, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start at QB in his place, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

players.outlook: Mike Washington has faded into a depth role in the Raiders' backfield. With Ashton Jeanty looking more effective on the ground, Washington has handled single-digit carries in three straight games, managing 62 rushing yards on 23 total totes. The rookie running back would likely need a Jeanty injury to get another shot at the top spot on early downs. Washington will face a Browns defense in Week 12 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Emanuel Wilson's role for Week 8 against the Bears could depend on whether Zach Charbonnet (knee) and/or Jadarian Price (chest) is ready to rejoin Seattle's backfield. As the Seahawks' lead RB in Week 7 against Kansas City, Wilson racked up 100 yards and a touchdown on a hearty 24 carries and added one catch for 15 yards. It was the third time over his past four contests that Wilson logged 20 or more totes, but should Charbonnet and/or Price be ready to return to the fold, Wilson will likely handle a reduced workload. Either way, he could find room to run against a Chicago defense that ranks 2

Chris Rodriguez could make a spot start for the Jaguars in a juicy Week 12 matchup against the 1-9 Titans if Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) sits out, in which case Rodriguez would have fantasy RB2 upside. If Tuten suits up, Rodriguez would remain in the deep-league flex conversation as Jacksonville's change-of-pace RB against a Tennessee defense that has allowed 44.7 points per game in its last three. The Jaguars scored 40 points against the Titans in Week 10, though Rodriguez was limited to a season-low five rushing yards in that game while Tuten racked up 113 scrimmage yards and a TD.

Ted Hurst will look to build on an impressive performance in Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Hurst was the Buccaneers' most productive receiver during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns. He also played 63% of the team's offensive snaps after playing just one the game prior, suggesting his role is growing as the year progresses. Despite this, Hurst could struggle in Week 12 against a Carolina secondary that's given up just 9.5 yards per reception this year, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.

Braelon Allen may garner enough work in the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins to be viable. Despite Breece Hall's return to health, Allen has at least eight carries in three straight games, with the Jets being run-centric. He found ample holes in the Dolphins' front as a lead back in Week 7 and can repeat that per-touch success, worthy of flex consideration.

Samaje Perine and the Bengals return home to host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He had six carries for 26 yards and caught all four targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Perine finished with one fewer touch than starter Chase Brown, but Perine was much more productive. Perine could be a sneaky fantasy play versus a New Orleans defense allowing 28.5 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing RBs.

J.K. Dobbins has faded into a depth role in the Broncos' backfield with the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins has handled single-digit touches in four straight games, and in a Week 11 win over the Raiders, he saw only one snap on offense, gaining zero yards on his only carry. The veteran's main path to fantasy relevance was through volume, and that no longer appears to be open while Coleman is healthy and effective. Dobbins will try to win back a little more work in Week 12 against a Steelers defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

news.text: The Broncos placed Dobbins on the reserve/suspended list Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.. Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. players.outlook: Cam Ward has thrown for at least 231 yards and two TDs in three consecutive games after failing to hit either of those passing benchmarks in any of his first seven starts this season. The 2025 first overall pick is growing in confidence, and he's also being forced to air it out as the 1-9 Titans consistently play catch-up. That's unlikely to change in Week 12, when the Titans face a Jaguars team that can put up points in bunches and is better at stopping the run than the pass. Ward's recent uptick in production has him in the conversation as a starter in superflex leagues, but there remain ple

Tommy DeVito doesn't inspire much confidence heading into the Patriots' Week 12 matchup with the Chargers. Taking over as the starter for Drake Maye (foot), DeVito will have Week 11's bye to prepare. However, he failed to impress when forced into duty in Week 10, throwing for just 81 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in three-plus quarters. The Chargers have allowed 16 touchdown passes through 10 games and a modest 7.8 yards per attempt, but a run-heavy approach seems more likely for the Patriots. DeVito is at or near the bottom of quarterback options.

Fernando Mendoza is beginning to show why he was the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. In the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, the rookie quarterback threw his first three career touchdown passes, and he did it without Brock Bowers in the lineup. Instead, Jack Bech emerged as his top target, while Mendoza's other two scores went to depth tight end Ian Thomas and running back Ashton Jeanty. Mendoza will look to secure his first win as a starter in Week 12 against a Browns defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth

news.text: Hurts (calf) is expected to be held out of football activities for multiple months and miss the rest of the season after new imaging over the weekend revealed several blood clots in his lungs, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.. Initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot after being cleated in the left calf in an Oct. 4 loss to the Rams, Hurts had been cleared by doctors to play in Week 5 in the Eagles' loss to the Jaguars in London before more recent testing last week showed that the blood clot had moved. According to a statement released Monday by his agent, Nicole Lynn, Hurts now has been diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis in the left calf, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli.

players.outlook: Corey Kiner brings double-digit touch potential into the Patriots' Week 12 game against the Chargers, as New England will likely run often with Tommy DeVito playing quarterback. The Chargers are allowing a modest 4.1 yards per carry but 10 touchdowns to running backs in 10 games, and six have topped 50 yards over the last five games. Kiner's lack of involvement in the passing game, paired with facing many eight-man fronts, tempers optimism, but opportunity should be available.

Audric Estime is expected to remain New Orleans' top short-yardage back in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Estime was inefficient in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, rushing seven times for six yards. It's a positive sign for Estime's fantasy outlook going forward that he still had a valuable role in New Orleans' offense, despite the return of lead-back Travis Etienne. However, Estime will likely have minimal fantasy value without finding the end zone. He's set to face a solid Bears defense that's given up just five rushing touchdowns to RBs this year.

George Holani and the Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown during Seattle's 17-14 loss in overtime in Week 6. Holani made the most of his touches by scoring his first rushing TD of the season, but he's expected to have his opportunities reduced with the likely return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) off the reserve/PUP list. It would be wise to steer clear of the Seahawks backfield against a Kansas City defense allowing 19.0 fantasy points allowed per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

Roschon Johnson will look to get back to full health as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Johnson hurt his ankle in the first quarter of Week 11 against the Saints and was unable to return to the matchup. While the return of Kyle Monangai was likely to diminish Johnson's role, he does have value as a change-of-pace option. IF he is able to return to the field, he'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

news.text: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out  for Thursday's game against the Lions.. Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

players.outlook: Tank Dell has just six catches for 48 yards in two games since his 105-yard outburst in Week 9, which included a 63-yard touchdown catch. A Week 12 home game against the Ravens offers Dell a chance to showcase his ability to generate big plays, as Baltimore's struggling defense has allowed at least 33 points to four of its last five opponents. Dell has a high enough ceiling to warrant flex consideration in most formats, though his floor remains shaky as he competes for targets in a deep Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte (hip), and Marvin Harrison

Bam Knight appears to be working in a RB timeshare for the Cardinals ahead of a Week 12 clash against the Commanders. Knight logged eight touches for 45 yards in this past Sunday's loss to Kansas City, while Tyler Allgeier finished with seven touches for 23 yards. Neither back has forced his way into a workhorse role, and rookie Jeremiyah Love could be on the verge of returning from an ankle injury, so Arizona's backfield is tough to get a read on at the moment. The team's running game also doesn't have the greatest Week 12 matchup, as Washington ranks in the top half of the league with 16.4 f

Elijah Mitchell led the Eagles in rushing last game. Jaydon Blue was initially thought to be the primary backup to Saquon Barkley, but it was Mitchell who led the Eagles with 34 yards on the ground. In fact, Blue did not even register a carry in the 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Barkley has been assured he will not be traded, leaving Blue as an afterthought, and perhaps even behind Mitchell on the depth chart. Meanwhile, a potentially juicy matchup is on the horizon in Week 9 versus the Giants for whomever is the bell cow. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the

Caleb Douglas is emerging as the top option in Miami's limited passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. He amassed a career-high 10 targets in Week 11 but brought in only two of them, finishing with 30 yards. The Dolphins have failed to reach the end zone through the air in two games with Kyle McCord at the helm, but Douglas brings volume into Week 12. He solved the Jets with two touchdowns and 70 yards on just two receptions in Week 7, but given McCord's volatility, lowering Douglas on your wide receiver depth chart is prudent in Week 12. Douglas is a high-upside WR/flex.

Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Will Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

news.text: The Eagles placed Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.. Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery for an abdominal injury that he picked up during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Giants. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also considered week-to-week, so with Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley could be the Eagles' starting running back for Week 5 against the Jaguars on Sunday in London.

players.outlook: Makai Lemon had a quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Lemon had just three looks for the game. Lemon finished with just one reception for three yards.  Brighter days could be ahead for Lemon, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

Puka Nacua is expected to miss the Rams' Week 10 clash against the Cardinals and several weeks beyond that. Nacua suffered a knee injury in this past Sunday's win over Washington and is likely to be placed on IR. Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR, so the Rams' WR corps will be led by the likes of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington.

news.text: Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his right MCL, which means he won't be on track to return at any point during the playoffs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.. Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mump

players.outlook: Sione Vaki will look to get more touches as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Vaki recorded some of his lowest usage of the season in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, rushing the ball once for negative-one yard and bringing in one target for seven yards. The third-year ball carrier has still logged five or more touches in three of his last four games, so hopefully he'll stay involved in the weeks to come. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked relatively middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this season.

Austin Ekeler had seven carries for 41 yards last game for Washington, though ceded the majority of touches out of the backfield to Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals, nearly doubling up Ekeler in terms of carries. Rachaad White dressed but did not play, likely due to a heel injury, so his status for Week 12 versus the Cardinals could also affect Ekeler's usage. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league, so there should be room to roam if Ekeler gets the opportunity.

Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

news.text: Doubs (shoulder), who remains on injured reserve, has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.. Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

players.outlook: Ryan Flournoy was not invited to the party last game for the Cowboys. While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each had over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown in the win over the Titans, Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards. It was his lowest output of the season. In Week 12, Flournoy will look to get back on track versus a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

Devin Singletary managed just two touches last game for the Giants. Singletary has just three touches over the last two contests, and even with starter Cam Skattebo fumbling, Singletary continues to serve mostly as depth. Singletary is also averaging just 2.9 yards per carry this season, which has not helped his cause. In Week 12, he could find some room to roam against the lowly Colts, though.  Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

Chris Brooks will look to stay involved in Week 12 as the Packers play the Rams. Brooks logged three touches in his return to the field against the Vikings before Green Bay's bye, but he converted them for just three total yards. The current backfield situation is crowded and underperforming, so it's hard to rely on any of Brooks, Kaleb Johnson or MarShawn Lloyd with or without Josh Jacobs active. Los Angeles has ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

Kaleb Johnson could lead Green Bay's backfield in a Week 12 matchup against the Rams. Johnson recorded double-digit carries in back-to-back games before the Packers' bye week, and he also logged first-team reps in the team's most recent Sunday practice. If Josh Jacobs remains out with a finger injury, Johnson may be the top option for the Pack in Los Angeles. The Rams have unfortunately ranked third in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

In Week 12, Michael Pittman and Pittsburgh aim to snap a two-game losing skid when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He hasn't played since Week 4 after being placed on injured reserve due to a foot injury, but the first-year Steeler is ready to make his return versus a talented Denver secondary, which is allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game to WRs. Pittman hasn't played in nearly two months, so fantasy managers needing help at receiver should look elsewhere until he can prove otherwise.

Pierre Strong could see an elevated role as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Strong logged eight carries for 22 yards and two catches for 11 yards in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, with MarShawn Lloyd and Josh Jacobs both dealing with injuries. The fourth-year ball carrier has served a change-of-pace role in his five appearances this season, but he could see even bigger usage if his position mates are inactive. Minnesota has ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

Dameon Pierce still managed to maintain a solid role despite the return of Saquon Barkley from injury for the Eagles.  Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown but tweaked his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. This allowed Pierce to take 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown of his own.  However, Pierce could be seen leaving the field late in the fourth quarter with a potential injury as well. If neither Barkley nor Pierce can play in Week 8 versus Washington, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back. The Commanders are allowing

news.text: The Eagles released Pierce (undisclosed) from IR with an injury settlement Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.. Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another o

players.outlook: Emari Demercado could play a significant role for the Texans in Week 11 against the Colts. Woody Marks (concussion) won't play, while David Montgomery is suting up Thursday for his first action since Week 5. Demercado's appeal is limited to deep-league flex status in a change-of-pace role, though Montgomery may not be ready to take on a full workload against a Colts defense that's surrendering 151 scrimmage yards and a touchdown per game to RBs. Demercado averaged 6.5 yards per carry on 126 attempts spread across three years with the Cardinals, but that figure has plummeted to 2.6 yards per ca

Josh Downs has seen very consistent usage in his two games with Kansas City, catching four passes on five targets in each with yardage in the 50s. The main difference was a touchdown in Week 10, something he wasn't able to repeat in a Week 11 win over the Cardinals. Downs is adapting quickly to his new offense, but Patrick Mahomes has plenty of other options in Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. Downs will look to continue building chemistry with Mahomes in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per g

Najee Harris had five carries for just nine yards last game for the Giants. The running game as a whole was fairly contained, as starter Cam Skattebo rushed for just 58 yards in the 27-27 tie with Washington. Interestingly, Tyrone Tracy also had five touches in this contest, perhaps showing that the backup role remains up for grabs. In Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.

Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle to make a big difference in the Broncos' passing game. In a Week 11 win over the Raiders, the former Dolphin caught three of six targets for 61 yards, his highest yardage total since Week 2. Waddle is on pace to record fewer than 700 receiving yards in a season for the first time, and with the Denver offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't had to air it out much. Waddle seems unlikely to break out in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Jaylen Wright remains minimally used in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. He played just nine offensive snaps in Week 11 rushing just five times for the fourth time in six games. While the Jets are allowing the eighth most fantasy points per game to running backs, Ollie Gordon dominates Miami's backfield. Wright lacks much fantasy appeal.

Omar Cooper's role in the Jets' offense remains inconsistent ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins, and his availability remains in question due to ankle and hip woes. Over his last five healthy games, Cooper has no catches in two of them and a combined 19 in the other three outings. He compiled 115 receiving yards and a touchdown against Miami earlier in the year, and their secondary is allowing 9.2 yards per target to receivers, the fifth-highest mark in the league. Cooper is a high-ceiling speculative play if he suits up.

news.text: Head coach Aaron Glenn announced Friday that Cooper (ankle/groin) will remain out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.. Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. players.outlook: In Week 12, DK Metcalf and the Steelers look to stay undefeated at home when they battle the Broncos on Black Friday. He caught one of four targets for two yards before being ejected in the third quarter of Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Metcalf's season continues to spiral out of control, and luckily for him, the veteran receiver will not face a suspension from the league following the scuffle. Metcalf will be on the field versus Denver, but he should remain on fantasy benches.

Michael Wilson could play in Arizona's Week 9 matchup against Seattle despite dealing with two broken ribs. The wideout suffered the injury this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, but he returned to the game after getting hurt and finished with eight catches for 111 yards and one touchdown on 15 targets. Wilson thrived with both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew under center, so the switch to Minshew as the Cardinals' starting QB shouldn't impact Wilson's production if he's able to suit up in Week 9. However, the ribs issue plus a stout Seattle pass defense that has given up the fewest fantas

news.text: The Cardinals placed Wilson (neck) on injured reserve Tuesday.. Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances

players.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will be inactive again in Week 12 as the Lions play the Bears. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

news.text: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.. Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

players.outlook: Will Shipley managed four touches last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley nursing a left arm injury for the final eight minutes of the win over the Steelers, Shipley saw four carries for nine yards. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. If Shipley is needed, he could have sneaky value against a Dallas defense that has been abysmal against the run in 2026.  The Cowboys are allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

A.J. Brown seems unlikely to play in Week 12 when the Patriots face the Chargers due to lingering hamstring issues. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams could see elevated roles, but with Tommy DeVito under center, all will be volatile options.

news.text: Brown (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.. With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first regular-season start at QB. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Dec. 6 against the Bills.

players.outlook: Kimani Vidal has remained a steady part of the Chargers' game plan in recent weeks. The third-year running back has handled at least eight touches in five of the last six games, managing 167 rushing yards and a touchdown over that stretch on 4.3 yards per carry while adding an 11-63-0 line on 15 targets. While Omarion Hampton has reasserted himself as the top back, a knee injury to Keaton Mitchell could reduce Vidal's competition for backup snaps. Vidal will try to take advantage of what volume he gets in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowe

Ray Davis has not been a part of the Bills' game plan entering a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. He has only two carries through four weeks, adding one catch while factoring in on kickoff returns. Seemingly losing snaps to Ty Johnson on passing downs in what was already a limited role, Davis's only fantasy appeal would be to James Cook managers in the event of an injury.

Ty Johnson looks to build on his modest production as a receiver out of Buffalo's backfield entering a Week 12 Thursday matchup with the Chiefs. He spiked in Week 11, snagging seven of eight targets for 55 yards, the third time he's reached 50 receiving yards in eight games. Johnson has only 33 touches on the season. With sporadic usage, he'll be hard to trust against a Chiefs defense that is allowing 4.5 catches to backs per game, but just 6.5 yards per target.

Kendre Miller is expected to operate as the Saints' top rusher in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) has been sidelined, Miller has averaged 11 carries per game, but just 28.8 rushing yards per game (2.6 yards per carry). Despite the lack of efficiency, Miller has led New Orleans' backfield in carries three consecutive games, which bodes well for his outlook while Etienne remains out. Miller could find success against the Browns' defense in Week 9, as they've given up 4.9 yards per carry to opposing running backs this season.

Brian Robinson (hamstring) is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Robinson has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a hamstring issue. However, he's been an effective runner when healthy, averaging 4.0 yards per carry and rushing for four touchdowns in six appearances this season. Despite this, he'll likely need to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant against a Bengals defense that's given up just 19.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.

news.text: Robinson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.. Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

players.outlook: Adonai Mitchell remains an inconsistent, high-upside option in the Jets' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Mitchell has three or fewer catches in four of five games since returning from a four-game injury absence, and the Jets have now failed to complete 20 passes for three straight games. Miami's secondary is vertically vulnerable, allowing 9.2 yards per target. The Dolphins are vulnerable to the run, and the Jets prefer to grind it out, so Mitchell will be a boom-or-bust option, likely excluding him from fantasy lineups.

Tyrone Tracy was the most productive back last game for the Giants, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown. However, he managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches overall. Meanwhile, Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches, Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries and Cam Skattebo did not even register a touch following last week's costly fumble. It will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. In Week 7, the Giants will also face a stingy Texans run defense.
