news.text: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.. The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

players.outlook: Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new

Seth McGowan injured his hamstring in the Colts' Week 11 loss to Houston and is expected to sit out Week 12 against the Giants. The rookie had been earning a larger share of carries in a change-of-pace role behind Jonathan Taylor. DJ Giddens moves up to the second spot on Indianapolis' RB depth chart, but he may not get as many opportunities as McGowan did.

news.text: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.. DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

players.outlook: Brenton Strange is a viable low-end starter at TE in Week 12 against the Titans, though Jacksonville's wideouts are more likely to find success versus Tennessee's leaky secondary. One of Strange's two TDs this season came in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he had a season-low nine receiving yards in that game. The Titans are holding TEs to 42 yards per game, though they have given up six TDs to the position. Strange ranks 14th at his position with 38 receiving yards per game.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

news.text: Hill's (knee) agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver hasn't yet been medically cleared but is expected to be "in a few weeks," James Palmer of Bleacher Report reports.. Though his outlook hasn't changed much since Rosenhaus last provided an update in mid-October, Hill is seemingly getting closer to being ready to take the field. It's unclear what type of interest Hill has garnered around the league, but he's a free agent and could hold some appeal for teams once doctors give him the green light to play.

players.outlook: In Week 12, Darnell Washington and the Steelers host Denver in an AFC clash on Black Friday. He caught all three targets for 22 yards during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Washington was unable to take advantage of Aaron Rodgers' 44 pass attempts, as the former has now been limited to 27 or fewer receiving yards in eight of his 10 outings. Washington remains a risky fantasy option despite a favorable matchup versus a Broncos defense allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to TEs

Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top wideouts during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Vele delivered a much-needed bounce-back performance during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, catching all seven of his targets for 76 yards. Despite playing behind Chris Olave, Vele appears to be a valuable portion of this New Orleans' offense and will likely compete for the No. 2 WR role with rookie Jordyn Tyson as the season progresses. Vele is still expected to struggle in Week 12 against a tough Bengals secondary that's given up just 10.2 yards per completion through nine games

Malachi Fields continued his streak of catching at least two balls in every game this season for the Giants. Fields had two receptions for 25 yards in the 23-18 win over the Jags. Fields received five targets for the game. The rookie is averaging a stout 15.6 yards per catch overall. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

Pat Bryant posted modest numbers over two games since returning from an ankle injury, catching seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The Broncos' passing game has been sluggish all year, and with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't been required to do too much through the air. Bryant seems to have good chemistry with the quarterback, giving him a stable floor even if his ceiling is TD-dependent. Bryant will try to stay busy in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Dalton Kincaid will need to overcome thumb and ankle injuries if he's to help the Bills in a promising Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. His playing time and production have slid over the last three weeks coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. Kincaid's snap share has dropped to around 50%, ceding his slot role to Dawson Knox, who is serving as an additional blocker on the line. If Kincaid plays, opportunities await, with Kansas City allowing tight ends to catch at least four passes in three straight games and five overall touchdowns. They have also yielded the seventh-most fantasy points per game

Mack Hollins is slated for an uptick in opportunity but with sketchy quarterback play when the Patriots face the Chargers in Week 12. He hauled in five catches for 48 yards in Week 10 despite losing Drake Maye on the opening drive and Tommy DeVito completing just 12 passes for 81 yards in relief. It's unlikely that DeVito airs it out, but with A.J. Brown (hamstring) likely out and the Chargers allowing 13 touchdowns and 9.1 yards per target to opposing wideouts, Hollins could surprise.

Tutu Atwell has a chance to buoy a depleted Rams wideout corps in Week 12 against Green Bay. Los Angeles will remain without both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the matchup, and Nacua isn't expected to return to action this year. However, Atwell wasn't effective when both star wideouts were absent Week 10 against the Cardinals, as he tallied just one catch for 31 yards on two targets. Atwell is always a big-play threat, though Green Bay has allowed just 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for seventh-fewest in the NFL.

Kayshon Boutte injured his hip in Week 11. Though the injury doesn't appear to be too serious, which suggests he could suit up in Week 12 against the Ravens, if Boutte plays, he'll be a high-risk, high-reward fantasy option best utilized in deeper leagues. He had 125 yards and two TDs in Week 9 against the Chargers, as well as 40 yards and a TD prior to getting hurt in Week 11 against the Colts, but Boutte has just 194 yards in eight other appearances for the Texans.

news.text: Boutte (hip) isn't practicing Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.. Wilson adds that Boutte isn't expected to play Sunday against the Ravens, and while things are certainly trending that way based on Boutte's inability to practice all week, that notion has yet to be confirmed by an official team source. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison will compete for playing time and targets alongside Nico Collins if Boutte is ruled out.

players.outlook: Michael Mayer wasn't able to take advantage of Brock Bowers' absence during the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, catching just one of four targets for a mere four yards. Depth tight end Ian Thomas also rubbed a little salt in the wound for Mayer's fantasy investors by catching a 19-yard touchdown from Fernando Mendoza. Bowers is expected back in Week 12, but even if he remains sidelined, Mayer's usage will make him a risky option, even against a Browns defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Dalton Schultz has been held to one catch for 11 yards in each of Houston's last two games, though one of those receptions was his first touchdown of the season. He has been utilized primarily as a blocker in Houston's recent games, so Schultz hasn't benefited much from the strong play of QB C.J. Stroud. In Week 12, Schultz will face a Ravens defense that has struggled to defend TEs, allowing 54 yards per game and seven TDs in 11 games to the position. He's a viable low-end starter at a position that lacks depth, but nobody's getting excited about starting Schultz these days.

news.text: Schultz (illness) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.. Schultz wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, which indicates that the illness is a new concern for the veteran tight end. A full session Friday would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens. Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), Foster Moreau and Marlin Klein would all be in line for larger roles on offense in the event that Schultz is not cleared to play in Week 12.

players.outlook: Quentin Johnston was nearly invisible again in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The fourth-year wideout has caught one pass in three straight games and five of his last six, as Mike McDaniel's quick-strike offensive scheme doesn't give him enough time to get downfield on the deep routes that have been his bread and butter. Johnston could be catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei instead of Justin Herbert due to the starting QB's concussion, but it's not like his outlook could get much worse. Johnston will try to take advantage of whatever target volume he gets in Week 12 against a Patriots

Mike Gesicki and the Bengals look to extend their three-game win streak at home versus the Saints in Week 12. He caught five of six targets for a team-high 77 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Gesicki finished third on the team in targets and matched Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown for the team lead in receptions. The outing was impressive considering Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes and threw for 300 yards, with Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) and Tee Higgins (2-43-1) combining for only 74 of them. Gesicki will attempt to punish a New Orleans defense allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game

Darius Cooper was the surprise leading receiver last game for the Eagles. Cooper managed four catches for a team-high 59 yards in the 19-16 win over the Steelers. He finished second on the team in targets for the contest, and only three other players caught passes from quarterback Joe Milton.  Cooper could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is expected to remain the Saints' top tight end if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Johnson sustained a hamstring injury during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, and the extent of the issue remains TBD. Johnson struggled to find fantasy value before sustaining this injury, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and one touchdown from Weeks 7 through 10 (three games). If active, Johnson could find fantasy value but is likely still too inconsistent to start, even with a favorable matchup against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy point

news.text: Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.. Johnson suffered a hamstring injury this past Sunday at Chicago, and he then was listed as a DNP on the Saints' first two Week 12 practice reports, despite head coach Kellen Moore calling the tight end "day-to-day" Thursday, according to Terrell. With Johnson missing his first game of the campaign and Noah Fant (calf) questionable for Sunday's matchup, Oscar Delp is the sole healthy player at the position on the active roster.

players.outlook: Chimere Dike has led Tennessee's wide receivers in receiving yards twice in the past three games, posting 71 yards in Week 8 against the Bengals and 69 yards in Week 11 against the Cowboys. He was held to just 16 receiving yards by the Jaguars in between, and Dike will face Jacksonville again in a Week 12 road rematch. He looks poised to remain a staple in three-receiver sets while working out of the slot since Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of the season. Dike has shown enough in recent weeks to earn flex consideration against a Jacksonville defense that is aro

AJ Barner heads into Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco amidst a stretch of consistent but quiet production. Barner has caught between two and four passes in each of his past six contests while averaging 21.2 receiving yards per game during that span. The third-year tight end actually has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving TDs (one) this season, as he's sometimes been deployed as a ball carrier in short-yardage situations. Barner posted a 3-20-0 receiving line on five targets against San Francisco in Week 5 during the teams' first meeting of the campaign. .

Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches in Week 12 to capitalize on facing a league-worst Titans secondary that's giving up 16 catches for 210 yards per game to WRs. He has caught multiple passes just twice all season for the Jaguars while growing into one of the league's best cornerbacks on the other side of the ball. With Jacksonville's WR room healthy entering Week 12, expect Hunter to be limited to a handful of snaps on offense as usual.

Jack Bech continues to show intriguing chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. In two games since Mendoza replaced Kirk Cousins under center, Bech has turned 16 targets into a 10-98-1 line with most of that production coming in a Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The second-year wide receiver missed four games earlier this year with a forearm injury but he appears to be fully recovered and ready to flash the upside that made him a third-round pick in 2025. Bech will face a Browns secondary in Week 12 that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Rashod Bateman and the Ravens look to snap a six-game losing streak when they visit the Texans in Week 12. He hauled in two of six targets for 67 yards, including a 52-yard touchdown, during Baltimore's Week 11 defeat. Bateman finished second on the team in yardage and targets, but he's now tallied three or fewer receptions in six straight outings. Despite a great matchup against Houston's vulnerable secondary, Bateman should remain on fantasy benches.

Dontayvion Wicks could return from an ankle issue for the Eagles following their bye. Wicks has missed three-straight games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of DeVonta Smith, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

news.text: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.. Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

players.outlook: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

news.text: McMillan (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.. McMillan has missed the Buccaneers' last seven games while recovering from an MCL sprain in his left knee that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 3. He was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and even if he practices in full over the next two days, he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Monday's game against the Panthers.

players.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq's usage remains inconsistent ahead of the Jets' Week 10 matchup with the Bills. While Sadiq flashed with four catches in Week 9, he previously had only five grabs in his previous five games despite the Jets throwing more than 30 times in each outing. Sadiq remains high on potential but low on opportunity, suggesting a volatile ceiling/floor against a defense that's allowed only one opposing tight end to score.

De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

news.text: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.. Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't ap

players.outlook: Tyler Higbee could be an important part of the Rams' passing game against the Packers in Week 12. Higbee hasn't exceeded 17 receiving yards in his past four games, but he did catch a touchdown in his most recent appearance, Week 10 against Arizona. The Rams continue to be without star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring), so it's been all-hands-on-deck for the team's pass catchers. However, Green Bay has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 5.9 fantasy points per game -- fifth-best in the league -- to the position.

news.text: Higbee (chest) is considered week-to-week, though it is too early to tell if he may be available Thursday, Dec. 3 against the Chiefs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports Friday.. Higbee and Davis Allen (ankle) were both injured during Wednesday's win over the Packers. Allen is likely facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, but Higbee still has a chance to avoid missing additional action. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are the only healthy TE options remaining for the Rams.

players.outlook: Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching d

Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns

news.text: McLaurin (knee) underwent surgery Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.. The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.

players.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Raiders for a Week 12 clash on Sunday Night Football. He caught two of four targets for 74 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Jeudy did most of his damage on a 65-yard reception, helping him finish second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (91). Despite the big day, Jeudy has two or fewer catches in three straight games and should remain on waiver wires.

Treylon Burks was largely held in check last game for the Commanders.  Burks caught two passes for 30 yards in the 22-20 win over the Bengals. He finished tied for fourth on the team in targets. In Week 12, Burks will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

news.text: Burks (foot) was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report.. Burks has been listed on Commanders practice reports with a foot injury since Week 8, but he's missed only one contest (Week 9 against the Rams) in four chances during that span. Friday's report will determine if Burks has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Arizona.

players.outlook: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

news.text: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Ferguson (hamstring) won't be activated from injured reserve this season and will require surgery to address the ankle injury he aggravated in Week 3, Stu Jackson of the team's official site reports.. Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve

players.outlook: Hunter Henry is saddled with an unfavorable Week 12 matchup when the Patriots take on the Chargers. He has just three targets in each of New England's last three games. Tommy DeVito playing quarterback could lead to additional check-downs, but that wasn't the case in Week 10 against Detroit. The Chargers have allowed one touchdown to a tight end, though a league-high 9.4 yards per target. Still, Henry isn't set up for a productive effort.

Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco looking for his first big game of the campaign. Shaheed returned from a two-game absence to suit up against the Raiders in Week 10 but managed just one catch for eight yards on two targets. The speedy wideout doesn't yet have a receiving touchdown this season, and he's topped out at five catches and 66 yards, though he's added value with occasional carries and especially with his work as a punt and kickoff returner. Shaheed may be dependent on big plays to put up useful fantasy production, and the 49ers have given up just 27

Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' top pass-catching tight end during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite being overshadowed by Mitchell Evans (5-44-1) during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, Waller remains first amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (41), receptions (28) and yards (365). In his first game against the Buccaneers this season, Waller was targeted just twice but caught a 50-yard touchdown to salvage his fantasy day. He could thrive in Week 12, as Tampa Bay's defense has given up 15.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

news.text: Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday.. Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

players.outlook: Cooper Kupp continues to be touchdown-dependent for fantasy value heading into Seattle's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco. Kupp has two TD receptions over his past three games but has recorded just five catches for 73 yards on eight targets during that span. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating targets in Seattle's offense, there simply hasn't been much of an opportunity for the team's other pass catchers to regularly find success. The 49ers held Kupp to two catches for 15 yards in their first matchup in Week 5, and Kupp may need to find the end zone in Week 12 to make a tangible impact for

Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers battle the Broncos at home on Black Friday in Week 12. He caught all five targets for 39 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Freiermuth has recently been more involved on offense than fellow tight end Darnell Washington as Washington finished with a 3-22-0 line on three targets. Freiermuth remains a TD-or-bust fantasy option and he'll face a Denver defense that's allowed the third-most receiving yards (702) and eight TDs (T-27th) to opposing TEs in 2026.

Roman Wilson and the Steelers host the Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12. He corralled three of six targets for 43 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Wilson made his presence felt in his first game action since Week 5, as he finished second on the team in yardage and third in targets while playing 70% of the offensive snaps. Wilson will try to continue building rapport with Aaron Rodgers versus Denver's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to WRs.

Konata Mumpfield appears set for at least one more game as the Rams' de facto No. 1 wideout in Week 12 against Green Bay. Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season, and Davante Adams (hamstring) is slated to remain on IR this week, leaving Los Angeles' WR corps in the hands of Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith. Mumpfield was the most productive of the group in Week 10 against Arizona, posting three catches for 81 yards on four targets. He'll look to build more momentum against the Packers, who rank 23rd in the league with 22.1 fantasy points per game al

Elic Ayomanor was surprisingly quiet in Tennessee's 51-30 loss to Dallas in Week 11. Chimere Dike, Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate each had at least five targets and 58 yards, while Ayomanor settled for 27 yards on three catches in the first game after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on IR. Titans QB Cam Ward has been spreading the ball around, and Ayomanor had his moment in Week 10 with 79 yards on 10 targets against the Jaguars, but the second-year wideout hasn't exceeded three catches in any other game this season. Expectations should be tempered in the Week 12 road rematch against a Ja

Kalif Raymond remains a depth option in Chicago's passing offense ahead of Week 12 at Detroit. Raymond struggled to do much with four targets in a Week 11 win over New Orleans, converting them into one catch for 14 yards. The veteran has now caught just 7 of his 14 targets in the Bears' last four outings. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

Gavin Bartholomew will aim to stay involved in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Bartholomew logged another catch in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he reeled in just one of his three targets for five yards. While he's seen up and down targets this season, he has been an involved member of the offense nonetheless in most weeks. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.

Jake Bates will look to tighten up as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Bates was mostly solid in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, but he did miss a 53-yard field goal in the first quarter. Either way, the third-year boot has now converted 17 of 19 field-goal attempts and nailed all 33 of his XPAs across 10 games this season. He'll face a Chicago defense that's a tough second in fantasy points allowed to kickers this season.

Oronde Gadsden's role in the Chargers' offense is shrinking. In two games since David Njoku returned from IR, Gadsden has just one target, catching it for a seven-yard gain. Njoku and Charlie Kolar are both better blockers than Gadsden, and the second-year tight end isn't a good fit for Mike McDaniel's offense. Gadsden is unlikely to make any sort of contribution in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Eli Raridon is trending favorably ahead of the Patriots' Week 10 matchup against a Lions defense that struggles against tight ends. Raridon has collected at least four targets in three straight games, even with fellow tight end Hunter Henry healthy, and the Lions are allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. While still a secondary option in New England's passing game, Raridon can garner enough attention to be a viable option in a plus matchup.

Cairo Santos will enter a tough matchup as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Santos missed a PAT in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but he converted both of his field-goal attempts. The veteran kicker has now made two or more field goals in each of his last four games. He'll take on a Detroit squad that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to his position.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

Chris Boswell and the Steelers aim to improve to 5-0 at home when they host the Broncos in Week 12 on Black Friday. He went 3-for-3 on field goal attempts and drilled his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Boswell has now converted all of his field goals in consecutive games for the first time all season. The veteran kicker will try to stay perfect versus a Denver defense allowing 21.0 points per game through 10 outings.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

JJason Sanders continues to get multiple scoring opportunities for the Jets ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. For the fourth consecutive week and fifth time in six games, Sanders made at least two field goals, giving him 19 in that stretch to go with nine extra points. The outlier was a Week 7 matchup with Miami, as the Jets played from behind and chose not to kick. With Kyle McCord under center for Miami in Week 12, that's not a likely script, suggesting Sanders can again be busy against a defense allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to kickers.

David Njoku caught his first passes since Week 2 in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, hauling in two of four targets for 21 yards. The veteran tight end missed six games earlier this season with a fractured fibula, but now that he's healthy, Njoku could offer the best mix of pass-catching ability and blocking skills at his position. Charlie Kolar, who is primarily a blocker, remains the starter, while big slot Oronde Gadsden is struggling to get on the field in Mike McDaniel's offense. Njoku will face a tough test in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that ranks fourth in fantasy points

Greg Dulcich has been unable to take advantage of favorable matchups as the Dolphins prepare for their Week 12 tilt with the Jets. He tied a season-high with seven targets in Week 11 but pulled in only two for 12 yards. He has yet to score and posted only two outings of 50 or more yards this season. One was against the Jets in Week 7, an 86-yard pop against a defense that's allowing a very targetable 8.1 yards per target to tight ends. Dulcich is a deep league streamer.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

In Week 12, Evan McPherson and the Bengals will attempt to extend a three-game home win streak when the Saints come to town. He went 2-for-2 on both field goal and extra point attempts during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. McPherson's 56-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining gave the Bengals the lead, but only for the time being, as their five-game win streak was snapped in the end. He bounced back nicely after missing his first kick of the season in Week 10, and McPherson will continue earning plenty of scoring opportunities in Cincinnati's high-powered offense.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if

Dawson Knox could benefit if he's again the Bills' top tight end with Dalton Kincaid's availability in question ahead of the Bills' Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Knox didn't garner much attention in Week 11 with Kincaid out, catching two of three targets for 31 yards. Even with more reps, his main job was blocking. Kansas City has been vulnerable to tight ends, allowing five touchdown receptions in 10 outings and the seventh-most fantasy points per game. If Kincaid misses Week 12's Thanksgiving affair, Knox becomes a deep league streamer.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

Tommy Tremble is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top tight ends during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite playing 82% of Carolina's offensive snaps during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, Tremble received minimal offensive work (1-18-0) while Mitchell Evans (5-44-1) and Darren Waller (3-42-0) excelled. Tremble still ranks second amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (35), receptions (26) and yards (245) through 10 games this year, but he likely shouldn't be relied upon as a fantasy starter. However, Tremble is in for a favorable Week 12 matchup against a Buccaneers de

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

Will Reichard will look to bounce back as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Reichard went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made one XPA in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Fortunately, those misses were just his second and third of the season, so there aren't currently any blaring warning signs of regression. He'll face a Falcons squad that's ranked top 10 versus fantasy kickers this campaign.

Colby Parkinson could be a big part of the Rams' passing game in Week 10 against Arizona. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles with four catches against Washington this past Sunday, though he gained just 13 yards on those receptions. Still, the Rams are going to need some pass catchers to step up in the wake of a knee injury that is likely going to cause star wideout Puka Nacua to miss multiple games, and Parkinson has tallied at least four catches in each of the last three games in which he's played. Matt Gay has been perfect over the last four weeks, going 5-for-5 on field goal attempts and 11-for-11 on PATs. The veteran kicker's volume hasn't been significantly affected by the switch at quarterback from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders' offense might actually take a step forward once Brock Bowers gets healthy, with young skill players Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech showing signs of breaking out. Gay will look to stay locked in during Week 12's clash with a Browns team that's allowing 22.0 points per game, tied for 14th in the league.

Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

Evan Engram is coming off his most productive game of the season in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders. The veteran tight end set new season highs in catches, targets, and receiving yards with a 6-74-0 line on eight looks from Bo Nix. However, Engram missed his chance to score his first touchdown since Week 1 when Adam Trautman vultured a one-yard TD on his only catch. Engram had managed just seven catches for 48 yards over his prior four games combined. He'll remain a volatile option in Week 12 against a Steelers defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Otton was underwhelming during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching just one of three targets for eight yards. He's tallied one-or-fewer receptions in four of the Buccaneers' last five games, making him almost impossible to trust for fantasy purposes going forward. Additionally, Otton is in for a tough Week 12 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 12.1 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

Gunnar Helm has topped 28 receiving yards only once all season and remains without a TD heading into the Titans' Week 12 trip to Jacksonville. He remains a non-factor in the vast majority of fantasy formats. The Jaguars are holding TEs to a league-low 34.3 yards per game, though they have allowed the position to score five TDs in 10 games.

Chase McLaughlin could receive few scoring chances during Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal during the Week 11 loss to the Lions but converted on all three of his extra points. On the season, the veteran has been perfect, making all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 21 of his point-after attempts. Despite his impressive season, Carolina has held opponents to just 7.1 kicking points per game, making this an unfavorable matchup for McLaughlin.

Harrison Butker appears to be taking the threat to his job security seriously. The veteran kicker has been perfect over the last two weeks, converting both his field goal attempts and all nine of his PATs. He had missed seven FGs in 10 games, although six of those shanks have come from 50-plus yards out. With the Kansas City offense ramping up its efficiency, Butker's volume is likely to skew more toward extra points, giving him a safer floor at the expense of his ceiling. He'll look to stay locked in during a Week 12 clash with a Bills team that ranks ninth in points per game allowed.
